ideas.body: Why did the librarian propose discussing a few notes with students before deciding whether to continue the programme?
What did the librarian propose doing before deciding whether to continue the programme?
What provision did the committee make for meetings lasting more than thirty minutes?
Which feature of the first trial did the organisers intend to address by proposing a same-day second trial?
While the organisers considered a second trial, what does the account state about the two map versions?
What limitation of the first trial is explicitly identified?
Which conclusion about the first trial is best supported by the passage?
Which feature was identical in the two map versions?
Which statement is explicitly reported about the cups lent by the canteen?
Which pattern in disposable-cup use did the report record across the two weeks?
What arrangement accompanied the washable cups lent during the second week?
After a letter confirmed one visitor’s identification, how did the archive handle that record?
What reason does the passage give for several visitors' initial dislike of the archive's distinction?

A volunteer offers a confident recollection identifying a photograph. No dated label or accompanying document identifies its subject, and no later corroborating material is available. How should the archive initially record the identification?

ideas.body: Why did Mira remain at the workshop until the radio’s wooden case was ready?
What did Mira do when rain began during the journey home?
After deciding she could reach home in time if she left immediately, what did Mira do?
Which action did Rohan take to help the pupil while continuing with his own task?

Which inference is best supported by Rohan’s response?
A. Asking another person to help can itself be a useful way to assist.
B. A person can assist only by carrying out the search personally.
C. An assigned task should be left unfinished whenever someone needs help.
D. Assistance is useful only after the person in need has solved the problem.
Before accepting the corrected score, what did the captains do?

Which account best describes how the captains reached and implemented their decision?
A. The captains accepted Dev's correction without checking the recorded deliveries.
B. The captains replayed the match before changing the recorded result.
C. The captains checked the deliveries but kept the original result unchanged.
D. The captains checked the deliveries, agreed on the correction, and changed the result without replaying the match.
Which elements did Amina retain in the shortened speech?
What can be inferred from Amina’s revision of her speech?
During the next attempt, what did Nisha do that enabled her to hear the flute’s quieter phrases clearly?
Which statement best captures the contrast between Nisha’s next group attempt and her later solo rehearsal plan?

Which conclusion is best supported by Nisha’s choices about pace?
She adjusted the pacing for group playing but kept the faster version for solo practice.
She adopted the drummer’s steady pace for both group playing and solo practice.
She discarded the faster version once it proved unsuitable for group playing.
She changed many notes so the flute’s quieter phrases could be heard.
What distinction does Nisha make in her response to the classmate’s praise?

ideas.body:
Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) This identification illustrates the two-part structure stated at the beginning.
(B) In it, “He” is the noun phrase (subject), while “acceded to demands for his resignation” is the verb phrase.
(C) All clauses in English have at least two parts: a noun phrase (subject) and a verb phrase.
(D) For instance, consider the clause “He acceded to demands for his resignation.”
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) The verb phrase is the other of these parts.
(B) Both categories named above belong to the structure of every English clause.
(C) Every English clause has at least two parts.
(D) Among these parts, the noun phrase is the subject.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences to form the unique coherent account. All four sentences describe the same wooden bookmark.
(A) After smoothing its edges, Noor painted the wooden bookmark and left it to dry.
(B) She used the drawing as a guide to cut the shape.
(C) Once the shape had been cut, she smoothed its edges.
(D) Noor first drew a design for a wooden bookmark.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) Each member then practised the assigned part individually.
(B) Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together.
(D) After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
(A) C-A-D-B
(B) D-C-A-B
(C) C-D-A-B
(D) C-D-B-A

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) She then attached the cut sheet to the board and let the adhesive dry.
(B) In a fictional class project, Tara first measured the width of the display board.
(C) Only after the adhesive had dried did she arrange the photographs on the covered board.
(D) Using that measurement, she cut a sheet of paper to fit the board.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) After editing it, he compared the copy with the untouched original.
(B) In this fictional account, Aman found that the recording of his interview contained background noise.
(C) He then edited the copy to reduce the noise.
(D) He first made a copy of the original recording.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Rearrange the following four sentences to form a coherent account:
(A) After those votes had been counted, the teacher wrote the selected title on the story's cover.
(B) She collected their proposals and then read the complete list aloud.
(C) The process began when the teacher asked pupils to suggest titles for a shared story.
(D) Only after hearing that list did the class vote on the titles it contained.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The four sentences below report one fictional rehearsal; arrange them in the order in which the events are reported.
(A) Each member then practised the assigned part individually.
(B) Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together.
(D) After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences about the same wooden bookmark to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) After smoothing them, she painted the bookmark and left it to dry.
(B) Once the shape had been cut, she smoothed its edges.
(C) In a fictional workshop, Noor first drew a design for a wooden bookmark.
(D) She used the drawing as a guide to cut the shape.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent account. Treat the temporal expressions in the sentences as explicit ordering cues.
(A) Only after writing the recorded name on a new label did Jaya replace the unreadable label.
(B) After checking the garden's planting record and finding the recorded name, Jaya wrote it on a new label.
(C) Jaya first noticed that the plant's label had become unreadable.
(D) After noticing that the label was unreadable, Jaya checked the plant's identity in the garden's own planting record.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent account.
(A) After editing the copy, Aman compared it with the untouched original.
(B) First, Aman made a copy of the original interview recording.
(C) He then edited that copy to reduce the background noise.
(D) Finally, Aman saved the edited version under a different name, while retaining the original throughout.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences from one fictional class project in the order that makes their references and timing cues coherent.
(A) Tara then attached the cut sheet to the board and let the adhesive dry.
(B) She used that measurement to cut a sheet of paper to fit the display board.
(C) Only after the adhesive had dried did Tara arrange the photographs on the covered board.
(D) In a fictional class project, Tara first measured the width of the display board.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences from a fictional account in a coherent order.
(A) The account concludes with a note that this sequence establishes the order of Jaya's actions without making an outside claim about the plant itself.
(B) In the fictional account, Jaya first noticed that a plant's label had become unreadable.
(C) Having found the recorded name, she wrote it on a new label.
(D) After noticing this, she checked the plant's identity in the garden's own planting record and found its recorded name.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent account.
(A) Each member then practised the assigned part individually.
(B) Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts.
(D) At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The four sentences below describe stages in one fictional account. Arrange them in chronological and referentially coherent order.
(A) Before opening the parcel, Ravi checked its address against the class's order receipt.
(B) After counting the notebooks, he recorded the count on the receipt and placed them in the cupboard.
(C) Ravi received a sealed parcel addressed to his class.
(D) Once he had confirmed that the address matched the receipt, Ravi opened the parcel and counted the notebooks inside.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences in the order in which the events are reported.
(A) Each participant practised the assigned speaking part individually.
(B) Finally, the group performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) The group first read a short scene together.
(D) After that reading, the group assigned its speaking parts.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
(A) C-D-A-B
(B) D-C-A-B
(C) C-A-D-B
(D) C-D-B-A

Arrange the following four sentences from one fictional account in a coherent order. Treat the sentence referring to the “stated process” as a concluding observation.
(A) He first made a copy of the original recording.
(B) The original was retained throughout the stated process.
(C) He then edited the copy to reduce the noise.
(D) In this fictional account, Aman found that the recording of his interview contained background noise.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The following four complete sentences describe one fictional class project. Arrange them in the order that makes their references and timing cues coherent.
(A) Only after the paper covering was attached and the adhesive had dried did Tara place the photographs on the board.
(B) Tara began by measuring the display board's width.
(C) She used that measurement to cut paper to fit the board.
(D) She attached the cut paper to the board and waited for the adhesive to dry.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The following four complete sentences describe one fictional account. Arrange them in the order that forms a coherent account.
(A) Only after comparing the edited copy with the untouched original did Aman save the edited version under a different name.
(B) Aman found background noise in the recording of his interview.
(C) He first made a copy of the original recording.
(D) He reduced the noise by editing that copy.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences to form a coherent account.
(A) Only then did the class vote on the listed titles.
(B) In a fictional class, the teacher first asked pupils to propose titles for a shared story.
(C) After the votes had been counted, she wrote the selected title on the story's cover.
(D) She collected their proposals and read the full list aloud.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The four sentences below report events in a single fictional rehearsal. Arrange them in the order that makes their temporal and referential links coherent. The account reports this order; it does not prescribe a procedure for all rehearsals.
(A) The shared reading was followed by assignment of the speaking parts.
(B) Once the parts had been assigned, each member practised the role individually.
(C) At this fictional rehearsal, the group began by reading a short scene together.
(D) After the individual practice, the group performed the scene together, using the parts its members had practised.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences from one fictional account in chronological and referentially coherent order.
(A) After locating the name in the record, Jaya wrote it on a fresh label.
(B) Jaya first noticed that the plant's existing label could no longer be read.
(C) She exchanged the unreadable label for the fresh one.
(D) To identify the plant, she consulted the garden's planting record.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences in a coherent order.
(A) After that shared reading, the group assigned the speaking parts.
(B) As a concluding qualification, the account reports this order for one fictional rehearsal; it does not prescribe it for every rehearsal.
(C) The group first read a short scene together.
(D) Before the group’s final performance, each member practised the assigned part individually; they then performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the four sentences from one fictional account in the order that follows the events described.
(A) Finally, Aman saved the edited version under a different name.
(B) Aman found that his interview recording contained background noise.
(C) After editing the copy to reduce the noise, he compared it with the untouched original.
(D) After finding the background noise, Aman made a copy of the original recording.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The following four complete sentences describe one fictional class project. Arrange them in a coherent order.
(A) Tara placed the photographs on the board after the adhesive had dried.
(B) She used the measured width to cut paper to fit the display board.
(C) After cutting the paper, Tara attached it to the board and let the adhesive dry.
(D) Tara's first step was to measure the width of the display board.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The four sentences describe Jaya’s actions in one fictional account. Arrange them in a coherent order.
(A) With the plant’s recorded name available, Jaya wrote it on a new label.
(B) Jaya first noticed that the plant’s label had become unreadable.
(C) She checked the plant’s identity in the garden’s own planting record.
(D) Only after writing the new label did she replace the unreadable one.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences from one fictional school event in a coherent order.
(A) With all the groups’ replies in hand, the organiser prepared the seating list.
(B) The volunteers used that completed list to place the chairs.
(C) After the volunteers had placed the chairs, the organiser checked the completed physical layout against the groups’ replies.
(D) The organiser began by asking each group how many chairs it needed.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences from one fictional account in the order in which the events occurred.
(A) After confirming the address matched the class's order receipt, Ravi opened the parcel and counted the notebooks inside.
(B) Finally, Ravi recorded the count on the receipt and placed the notebooks in the cupboard.
(C) Ravi received a sealed parcel addressed to his class.
(D) Before opening the parcel, he checked its address against the class's order receipt.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the four sentences from one fictional workshop account in the order that makes their stated references and timing coherent. All four describe the same bookmark, and each later action follows the preceding one.
(A) After smoothing the edges, Noor painted the bookmark and left it to dry.
(B) Once the shape had been cut, Noor smoothed its edges.
(C) Noor first drew a design for a wooden bookmark.
(D) Using that drawing as a guide, Noor cut the bookmark's shape.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Arrange the following four sentences from one fictional account in the order that makes their references and timing coherent.
(A) She then smoothed the edges of the shape just cut.
(B) Using that drawing as a guide, Noor cut the bookmark's shape.
(C) After that smoothing, she painted the bookmark and left it to dry.
(D) In a fictional workshop, Noor first drew a design for a wooden bookmark.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The following sentences describe events in a fictional class project. Arrange them in chronological order.
(A) Tara attached the cut sheet to the board and let the adhesive dry.
(B) Tara first measured the width of the display board.
(C) Only after the adhesive had dried did Tara arrange the photographs on the covered board.
(D) Using that measurement, Tara cut a sheet of paper to fit the display board.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

ideas.body:
Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Benevolent
(B) Candid
(C) Coherent
(D) Concise

List-II
(I) Giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words
(II) Logical and well organised; easy to understand and clear
(III) Kind, helpful and generous
(IV) Saying what you think openly and honestly; not hiding your thoughts

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Mira’s report contains only the essential points.
(B) Dev states his opinion openly and does not hide it.
(C) The ideas in the explanation are arranged logically and are easy to understand.
(D) Ravi is kind to others and readily offers help.

List-II
(I) Benevolent
(II) Candid
(III) Coherent
(IV) Concise

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each word in List-I with its meaning in List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) "reluctant"
(B) "assertive"
(C) "discreet"
(D) "transient"

List-II
(I) careful in what you say or do, in order to keep something secret
(II) hesitating before doing something because you do not want to do it
(III) continuing for only a short time
(IV) expressing opinions or desires strongly and with confidence, so that people take notice

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation with the part of the meaning of "arrogant" that it most directly illustrates.

List-I
(A) A person boasts about their own status but otherwise treats people considerately and courteously.
(B) A person speaks offensively but neither claims superiority nor disregards other people’s needs.
(C) A person makes a decision without considering its effect on others, but does not boast or speak offensively.
(D) A person boasts of being superior, speaks offensively and ignores other people’s concerns.

List-II
(I) Showing little thought for other people
(II) Behaving in a proud way
(III) Behaving in an unpleasant way
(IV) The complete meaning of "arrogant"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the adjective in List-II that best describes it. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A journey that demands a lot of effort and energy over several days
(B) A person careful in speech to keep a private matter secret
(C) A speaker who expresses an opinion strongly and confidently so that people notice
(D) A donor who is kind, helpful and generous

List-II
(I) Benevolent
(II) Arduous
(III) Assertive
(IV) Discreet

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A reply is aggressive or unfriendly, and its speaker is ready to argue.
(B) An event occurs only occasionally, at irregular intervals.
(C) A household uses only as much money as is necessary.
(D) An item is known to be genuine and not a copy.

List-II
(I) Hostile
(II) Sporadic
(III) Frugal
(IV) Authentic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) During a discussion, Sam responds in an aggressive, unfriendly way and seems ready to argue.
(B) An explanation for missing a meeting seems reasonable and likely to be true.
(C) Lee behaves proudly and unpleasantly, showing little thought for others.
(D) Mira openly and honestly says what she thinks without hiding her thoughts.

List-II
(I) Candid
(II) Hostile
(III) Plausible
(IV) Arrogant

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) "Obsolete"
(B) "Benevolent"
(C) "Optimistic"
(D) "Plausible"

List-II
(I) Expecting good things to happen or something to be successful; showing this feeling
(II) Kind, helpful and generous
(III) (of an excuse or explanation) reasonable and likely to be true
(IV) No longer used because something new has been invented

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each person's described behaviour in List-I with the adjective in List-II that best fits it. Use only the behaviour stated in each description.

List-I
(A) Riya checks each entry carefully and corrects mistakes to ensure that her work is done correctly.
(B) Dev feels very happy and excited after receiving good news.
(C) Meera watches carefully for signs of danger during a walk.
(D) Arjun behaves in a proud, unpleasant way and shows little thought for other people.

List-II
(I) Vigilant
(II) Arrogant
(III) Elated
(IV) Conscientious

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once. The stated necessary amount in each case is the amount required for that person's stated need.

List-I
(A) Leena takes 1 portion of food when 1 portion is necessary for her meal.
(B) Omar uses ₹40 when ₹40 is necessary for his task.
(C) Nisha takes 2 portions of food when 1 portion is necessary for her meal.
(D) Ravi uses ₹60 when ₹40 is necessary for his task.

List-II
(I) Uses only the necessary amount of money
(II) Uses more food than is necessary
(III) Uses only the necessary amount of food
(IV) Uses more money than is necessary

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Offers help and gives generously.
(B) Shows no interest in a discussion.
(C) States an opinion strongly and confidently so that others take notice.
(D) Shares thoughts openly and honestly.

List-II
(I) "Assertive"
(II) "Benevolent"
(III) "Candid"
(IV) "Indifferent"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) An excuse is reasonable and likely to be true.
(B) A decision is made sensibly and carefully, avoiding unnecessary risks.
(C) Only as much money or food as is necessary is used.
(D) An object is easy to see or notice and likely to attract attention.

List-II
(I) "frugal"
(II) "conspicuous"
(III) "plausible"
(IV) "prudent"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each message in List-I with the shorter restatement in List-II that preserves its essential information. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) The meeting that was planned for Monday has been moved to Tuesday.
(B) Please return the form to the office before 4 pm today.
(C) The shop will remain closed during the whole of Sunday.
(D) We need to collect signatures from all five group members.

List-II
(I) The shop will be closed all Sunday.
(II) Return the form to the office before 4 pm today.
(III) Collect all five group members' signatures.
(IV) Monday's meeting is now on Tuesday.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) After an unpleasant setback, Noor returns quickly to her usual functioning.
(B) A notice gives the necessary date, venue and action in a few short lines, without unrelated background.
(C) An explanation presents its ideas in a logical order and is easy to understand.
(D) A reply is aggressive and ready to argue.

List-II
(I) Hostile
(II) Concise
(III) Resilient
(IV) Coherent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A notice gives readers the necessary details in a few words.
(B) Leena completes her assigned work with care and sustained effort.
(C) Only a few houses stand far apart across the plain.
(D) Before accepting the task, Noor hesitates because she does not wish to do it.

List-II
(I) Diligent
(II) Sparse
(III) Reluctant
(IV) Concise

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each action with the quality it demonstrates. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) An editor removes unnecessary wording while retaining the essential points and uses few words.
(B) A writer arranges the ideas logically so that the explanation is clear.
(C) A coordinator is able to handle writing, editing and layout.
(D) A proofreader checks each correction carefully and correctly.

List-II
(I) Conscientious
(II) Concise
(III) Coherent
(IV) Versatile

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each case in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes the stated action or preference. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Before sending a spreadsheet, Asha checks each figure and corrects any errors so that the work is done carefully and correctly.
(B) On a forest walk, Imran watches for signs of danger or trouble.
(C) In a brief notice, Tara uses few words and includes only necessary and important information.
(D) At a community gathering, Kabir enjoys being with other people.

List-II
(I) "gregarious"
(II) "conscientious"
(III) "vigilant"
(IV) "concise"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each case in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) An assistant shows care and effort in completing assigned duties.
(B) An auditor pays careful attention to every detail while checking a file.
(C) A staff member is able to perform many different kinds of tasks.
(D) A colleague is aggressive or unfriendly and ready to argue.

List-II
(I) "meticulous"
(II) "diligent"
(III) "hostile"
(IV) "versatile"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each description in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once. Use only the feature stated in each description.

List-I
(A) A person can design posters, repair bicycles, translate short texts, teach music and organise events.
(B) An object is known to be real and what it is claimed to be, rather than a copy.
(C) An explanation is logical, well organised and easy to understand.
(D) Plants are present in small numbers and spread over a large area.

List-II
(I) Coherent
(II) Versatile
(III) Sparse
(IV) Authentic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A staff member spends several weeks on a task that demands great effort and energy.
(B) When challenged, a colleague responds in an unfriendly way and seems ready to argue.
(C) At a gathering, a person enjoys being among other people.
(D) A training video is uninteresting and seems to go on for too long.

List-II
(I) "hostile"
(II) "gregarious"
(III) "tedious"
(IV) "arduous"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Use "coherent" to mean that ideas are logically organised and that the writing is easy to understand and clear. Each entry describes a report about a process; classify it using only these two features.

List-I
(A) The report presents the stages in an order that follows the process, and explains each stage clearly and in wording that is easy to understand.
(B) The report presents the stages in an order that follows the process, but the explanations are unclear and difficult to understand.
(C) The report presents the stages in an order that does not follow the process, but explains each stage clearly and in wording that is easy to understand.
(D) The report presents the stages in an order that does not follow the process, and the explanations are unclear and difficult to understand.

List-II
(I) Both features are present
(II) Only logical organisation is present
(III) Only clarity and ease of understanding are present
(IV) Neither feature is present

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A region has only a few villages, spread across a wide area.
(B) A person can perform many different kinds of tasks.
(C) A person recovers quickly after an unpleasant shock.
(D) A worker carries out duties with care and effort.

List-II
(I) "Diligent"
(II) "Sparse"
(III) "Resilient"
(IV) "Versatile"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the assessment in List-II. Match the person’s stated preference separately from whether the person is currently alone or with others.

List-I
(A) Asha joins an optional group gathering because she says she enjoys being with other people.
(B) Bilal works alone because his task requires him to work in a quiet room; he says he likes being with other people.
(C) Charu declines an optional group gathering and says she prefers spending time alone.
(D) Deepa attends a team meeting because participation is required; she says she prefers spending her free time alone.

List-II
(I) Likes company and chooses it voluntarily.
(II) Likes company but is alone because the task requires it.
(III) Prefers being alone and chooses it voluntarily.
(IV) Prefers being alone but joins others because participation is required.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

For the task in every case, the complete required message is: “Submit the signed form to Room 4 by noon.” Each detail in this message is necessary. Match each draft with the assessment that best describes it. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) “Submit the signed form to Room 4 by noon.”
(B) “Submit the signed form to Room 4 by noon. The office has blue walls.”
(C) “Submit the form to Room 4 by noon.”
(D) “Please submit the signed form to Room 4 by noon, and ensure that the signed form reaches Room 4 by noon.”

List-II
(I) Gives the necessary information in few words
(II) Adds information that is not needed for the stated purpose
(III) Leaves out information needed for the stated purpose
(IV) Repeats the same required information in extra words

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each case in List-I with the word in List-II that best fits the stated feature. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A troubleshooting guide arranges its instructions logically, making them easy to follow.
(B) A meeting record retains only necessary and important information, expressed in a few words.
(C) In a wide region, trees are present in small numbers and are spread far apart.
(D) A cartographer checks every symbol and label on a map, paying careful attention to each detail.

List-II
(I) "Concise" — giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words
(II) "Sparse" — only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area
(III) "Meticulous" — paying careful attention to every detail
(IV) "Coherent" — logical and well organized; easy to understand and clear

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each survey description in List-I with the profile in List-II that best fits it. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A survey records a small number of shrubs, distributed across the whole reserve.
(B) A survey records many shrubs, distributed across the whole reserve.
(C) A survey records a small number of shrubs, all within one corner of the reserve.
(D) A survey records many shrubs, all within one corner of the reserve.

List-II
(I) Many shrubs, spread over a large area
(II) "sparse": present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area
(III) A small number of shrubs, clustered in one part of an area
(IV) Many shrubs, clustered in one part of an area

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each word in List-I with its meaning in List-II.

List-I
(A) concise
(B) authentic
(C) sceptical
(D) sparse

List-II
(I) known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy
(II) giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words
(III) having doubts that a claim or statement is true or that something will happen
(IV) only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each case with the conclusion supported by the stated finding. Use each conclusion once.

List-I
(A) An item is catalogued as an original violin; examination confirms it is genuine and not a copy.
(B) An item is catalogued as an original violin; examination confirms it is a copy.
(C) An item is catalogued as a guitar; examination confirms it is a genuine violin, not a copy.
(D) An item is catalogued as an original violin; whether it is genuine or a copy is unverified.

List-II
(I) Genuine, as described, and not a copy
(II) Known to be a copy
(III) Genuine, but not as described
(IV) Genuineness or copying is unverified

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

For this question, “authentic” means “known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy”. Each document’s stated status is complete.

Match each document in List-I with its assessment in List-II. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Claimed to be original Report R; confirmed genuine, correctly identified as Report R and not a copy, but one statement inside is false.
(B) Claimed to be a copy of Report S; confirmed to be a copy.
(C) Claimed to be original Report T; confirmed genuine and not a copy, but established to be Report U, not Report T.
(D) Claimed to be original Report V; whether it is genuine and whether it is a copy are unverified.

List-II
(I) Authentic, though one statement is false
(II) Not authentic because it is known to be a copy
(III) Genuine, but not what it is claimed to be
(IV) Authenticity is not established

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each case with its status. The label in every case claims the item is a real Model P and not a copy. Treat each finding as complete.

List-I
(A) Verified real, identified as Model P, and not a copy
(B) Verified as a copy of Model P
(C) Verified real and not a copy, but identified as Model Q
(D) Whether it is real, Model P or a copy is unverified

List-II
(I) Known copy
(II) Authenticity not established
(III) Authentic as claimed
(IV) Real, but not as claimed

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each position to an assessment; use each assessment once. Treat each position as complete and literal.

List-I
(A) Doubts the claim that the sample is safe.
(B) Accepts the schedule but doubts that delivery by Friday will occur.
(C) Is certain that the sample is safe.
(D) Has no view on safety or delivery.

List-II
(I) Doubts a claim’s truth
(II) Doubts that an event will happen
(III) Is certain a claim is true
(IV) Expresses no view

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

“Sceptical” means “having doubts that a claim or statement is true or that something will happen”. Let P be a claim. Match each response with the stance it explicitly expresses. Use each conclusion once.

List-I
(A) “I doubt P is true, though it may be true.”
(B) “I doubt P is true; I say it is false.”
(C) “P is true; I have no doubts.”
(D) “I have not considered whether P is true.”

List-II
(I) Doubts P, but does not state that P is false
(II) Doubts P and states that P is false
(III) Accepts P as true without doubt
(IV) States no view on whether P is true

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

“Inquisitive” means “very interested in learning about many different things”. Match each case with its assessment. Treat each description as complete.

List-I
(A) Very interested in learning about art, science and languages.
(B) Very interested in learning about stars only.
(C) Very interested in art, science and languages, but not in learning about them.
(D) Interested in learning about art, science and languages, but not very interested.

List-II
(I) Fits the meaning
(II) Too narrow: one thing only
(III) Not interested in learning
(IV) Not very interested

ideas.body: Choose the word closest in meaning to "arrogant".
A caterer prepares only the quantity of food needed for a meal, and its use of food is described as “frugal”. Which phrase expresses an antonym of “frugal” in this context?

Choose the word closest in meaning to "conspicuous" in the sentence below.
Though the room was decorated in muted colours, the large gold clock above the doorway remained conspicuous.
Which word is closest in meaning to "hostile"?
Choose the phrase closest in meaning to "benevolent".
In the sentence, "Mira was diligent in carrying out her assigned duties," which phrase is closest in meaning to "diligent"?

An editor prepares two notices. Both are logical and well organised, prepared with equal care, and equally easy to see. The first gives only the information that is necessary and important, using few words. The second adds repeated wording and nonessential details. Which word names the first notice’s quality of giving only necessary and important information in few words, a quality the second lacks?
Choose the word that means "not supporting one person or group more than another".

Although Leena was resolute in carrying out her plan, she had been prudent in choosing it: she considered her options and avoided unnecessary risks. Which phrase is opposite in meaning to "prudent" as used here?

Choose the option closest in meaning to "prudent" in the sentence below.
Before approving the proposal, the treasurer took a prudent approach, weighing possible risks carefully.

After a sudden closure of her small business, Meera regained her confidence and returned to work soon. Her colleagues described her as "resilient". Which phrase is closest in meaning to "resilient" as used here?

Two reviewers considered an explanation for a late delivery. One found its wording ambiguous, and another remained sceptical; the lead reviewer called it plausible. Which phrase gives the closest meaning of "plausible" as used here?

Although hired as an illustrator, Nila also edits captions, prepares layouts and presents design ideas to clients. Her manager describes her as versatile. Which phrase is closest in meaning to "versatile" as used here?
The excitement proved transient: it faded before the meeting ended, whereas the committee’s resolve continued through months of setbacks. Which word is the best antonym of "transient" as used here?

The supplier predicted that its new system would halve a shop’s energy use. Mira asked for evidence before accepting the prediction and remained “sceptical”. Which word is closest in meaning to “sceptical” as used here?
At a public event, volunteers wore conspicuous badges so visitors could spot them quickly. Which word is the best antonym of "conspicuous" as used here?

During a night watch, Leena looked up from her notes at intervals and spotted a warning sign. She was praised as "vigilant", although she had not checked every detail of the log. Which phrase is the clearest antonym of "vigilant" in this context?

Before submitting the ledger, Mira checked each entry against the receipts and corrected every error. Her supervisor described her approach as “conscientious”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “conscientious” as used here?

A catalogue describes a seal as "authentic" when it is the real seal claimed by its label, rather than a copy. A second seal was made to pass as the seal described on its label, although it was not that seal. Which word is the best antonym of "authentic" in this context?

Mira had accepted the invitation to present the report, but when her turn came she kept postponing it and hoped a colleague would begin first. Mira was reluctant to present. Which word is closest in meaning to "reluctant" as used here?
A family was described as frugal after carefully limiting its grocery spending to the amount needed. Which word is closest in meaning to “frugal” in this sentence?

A reviewer says an outage could have been stopped by activating an available, working backup switch, and therefore rejects the report's description of it as "inevitable". Which word best expresses the antonym of "inevitable" in this context?
Although the report contains accurate information, its sections are not arranged logically and its explanation is hard to understand. Which word is the best antonym of “coherent” in this context?

Read the sentence and choose the option closest in meaning to "sparse" as used here.
Across the vast reserve, settlements were sparse: the survey found only a few villages, with long stretches of open land between them.

On a museum visit, Leena asks how fossils form, why different materials are used in the exhibits, and what questions researchers are investigating. Her guide describes her as “inquisitive”. Which word is closest in meaning to “inquisitive” in this context?
Mira’s colleague privately told her about an upcoming resignation. Mira was discreet and did not repeat the information to anyone else. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “discreet” as used here?

The dictionary definition supplied for this item describes "sparse" as "only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area." Consider only spatial distribution, not the number of stations. A set of stations spread over a large zone is redesigned so that the stations are packed closely together within a small part of that zone. Which adjective best expresses the spatial opposite of "sparse"?

In a review of a report, a student writes: “Each paragraph followed logically from the previous one, and the evidence led clearly to the conclusion. The report was coherent.” Which phrase is closest in meaning to “coherent” as used here?

At a community arts centre, Arjun teaches music, repairs equipment, and manages bookings. The centre describes him as "versatile" because he takes on these different duties. Which phrase is the antonym of "versatile" in this context?

At the end of a long review, the chair asked for a concise report that preserved the decision, the assigned action and the deadline, but left out repeated background. Which phrase is closest in meaning to "concise" as used here?
A dealer labels a vase as an original. After examining it, an appraiser concludes that it is authentic, not a copy. Which option is closest in meaning to "authentic" as used here?

Choose the word closest in meaning to "transient" as used in the sentence below.
The organisers described the mobile exhibition as transient: it occupied the foyer for one weekend and was then removed as scheduled.

During a debate, the moderator listened closely to both teams and applied the same speaking-time rule to each, without favouring either team. The report described the moderator as "impartial". Which phrase expresses the opposite of "impartial" as used here?

Choose the word closest in meaning to “tedious” as used in the sentence below.
Entering the same names into column after column took most of the afternoon. By the end, the volunteers were finding it hard to stay interested, and they described the task as tedious.

At a committee meeting, Dev states his preferred timetable firmly and confidently, and the members take notice. Isha says openly and honestly that she has not formed a preference and is not ready to recommend one. Which phrase best expresses the antonym of "assertive" in this context?

When asked why the parcel arrived late, Nikhil gave an explanation consistent with the dispatch log, which recorded that it had left the warehouse a day late. His explanation was described as "plausible". Which phrase is closest in meaning to "plausible" as used here?

Read the sentence and choose the phrase closest in meaning to “inevitable” as used here.
The village’s only road crossed a bridge that was closed for the day, and no alternative route was available. The delivery could not reach the village that day; a delay was inevitable.

At a review meeting, Mira is asked for her view of a proposal. She openly and honestly says that she opposes it. A second reviewer privately also opposes it but deliberately gives a vague reply so the group will not learn her actual view. Which phrase describes the second reviewer’s response as an antonym of “candid”?

A relief group is called "benevolent" because it treats recipients kindly, gives them practical help and offers generous support. Which phrase is the antonym of "benevolent" in this context, reversing all three qualities?

After hearing that most colleagues supported the proposal, Devika told the group that she thought its evidence was weak and explained her reasons. The chair described her response as “candid”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “candid” as used here?

At the residents’ club, Nisha willingly joins group meals and social activities and rarely chooses to spend her leisure time alone. Her friends describe her as “gregarious”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “gregarious” as used here?

During a confidential schedule change, Nila checked her notices for accuracy and kept them brief. She was discreet when she withheld the unpublished detail, but later carelessly posted it in a public group. Which phrase expresses the antonym of “discreet” as used here?
While reviewing an inventory, Sana checked each record and paid close attention to its details. Her supervisor described her work as “meticulous”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “meticulous”?

At a wildlife reserve, Sana kept watching the river level and the bank for signs that rising water might endanger the camp. Her team described her as “vigilant”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “vigilant” as used here?

Read the sentence and choose the phrase closest in meaning to “ambiguous” as used here.
After reading the line “They saw her duck,” one classmate said it meant that they watched her lower her head; another said it meant that they saw the bird belonging to her. The teacher described the line as ambiguous.

The archive assignment would take several hours and require checking many entries. Rina nevertheless requested it, saying she wanted to do it and needed no encouragement. Which phrase is the clearest antonym of "reluctant" in this context?

In a planning meeting, Dev clearly stated the outcome he wanted and explained his recommendation with confidence so that the group would take his view seriously. A colleague described Dev as “assertive”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “assertive” as used here?

At a design review, Meera presented her work confidently. She was described as “arrogant” because she claimed the team’s success as solely hers and dismissed her colleagues’ concerns. Which phrase best expresses an antonym of “arrogant” as used here?

An office stopped using its old filing device because a newly invented electronic system now performs the same task. The old device still works. Which word is closest in meaning to “obsolete” as used here?

A planning team needs a handover note containing the decision, the responsible person and the deadline. One draft preserves all three points but repeats background and adds nonessential details, making the note much longer than needed. Which word is the best antonym of "concise" for this draft?
When the results showed that her team had won the final, Riya felt “elated” and celebrated with her teammates. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “elated” as used here?

At a school book fair, students were asked which author they would like the organisers to invite. Nila showed no curiosity about the proposals and said the choice did not matter to her. Her teacher described her as indifferent to the invitation. Which option is closest in meaning to “indifferent” as used here?

After a sudden leak damaged their studio, the artists were initially unsettled. They repaired the space and resumed work soon afterwards. A review described their response as "resilient". Which option is the clearest antonym of "resilient" as used here?

For several weeks, the crew carried heavy supplies up a steep route each day, with little time to rest. The supervisor described the assignment as "arduous". Which word is closest in meaning to "arduous" as used here?

An archive still consults its paper index each day, although a newly invented digital index is available. The paper index is old and less convenient, but its use has not stopped. Which phrase best expresses the antonym of “obsolete” as used here?

At a community event, Leela actively seeks company and enjoys being with other people. Arun is very happy about the event’s success and checks its arrangements carefully, but he responds to others in an unfriendly manner and is ready to argue. Which word best expresses the contrast to Leela’s social trait when describing Arun’s manner toward others?
For this question, "authentic" means “known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy.” Which case satisfies this meaning?

Dev cared deeply about preserving the archive, but he entered accession labels hastily and left mismatches with the inventory uncorrected. Which adjective is the clearest antonym of "conscientious" as it applies to his method?
A dealer describes a manuscript as an author's original manuscript. Which case fits the meaning of “authentic”?

At a planning meeting, Ravi disagreed with a proposal. He spoke aggressively, treated the other members in an unfriendly way, and showed that he was ready to argue. The question concerns his manner, not his opinion of the proposal. Which phrase best expresses an antonym of "hostile" as used here?

During a review, Leena checked each assigned record carefully, corrected errors and persisted until the work was complete. Her colleague was given the same duties but showed no interest in them. Which word best expresses the antonym of "diligent" as used in this context?
Which definition best matches the word "gregarious"?

While preparing stock records, Riya skipped the required checks, left visible mistakes uncorrected, and submitted entries without verifying them. Which word best describes her approach as an antonym of “conscientious”?
The team’s arduous assignment demanded sustained effort and energy over several weeks. Which word is the clearest antonym of “arduous” as used here?
Even after the first attempt failed, Nila expected the revised plan to succeed. Which word is closest in meaning to “optimistic” as used here?

A meticulous proofreader pays careful attention to every detail. Another proofreader skips detail checks and overlooks errors. Which word is the antonym of “meticulous” for the second proofreader’s method?
A committee chair reviews proposals from two competing teams, applies the same criteria to each, and favours neither. Which word is closest in meaning to "impartial" as used here?
During a group activity, Nina enjoys being with the other participants, whereas Omar shows no interest in them. Which word is the antonym of "gregarious" as used to describe Nina?

A single sensor logged a large number of alerts—60—in one hour, but the gaps between alerts varied rather than following a fixed interval. The report called this pattern “sporadic”. Which word is closest in meaning to “sporadic” here?
Before the results were announced, Noor expected her project to succeed, although she was not especially happy or excited. Which listed adjective conveys her expectation of success?

ideas.body: Assume that a report’s key findings are the only information necessary and important. Choose the sentence in which “concise” is used correctly to mean giving only necessary and important information, using few words.
Choose the sentence in which “conscientious” is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which “coherent” is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which “candid” is used correctly.

A library replaces its card catalogue with a newly developed, searchable digital catalogue and stops using the card catalogue. The old card catalogue is therefore ____.

Which word best completes the sentence?
Choose the sentence in which “assertive” is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which "conspicuous" is used to mean easy to see or notice and likely to attract attention.
Choose the sentence in which “sporadic” is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which "versatile" is used in the supplied sense of a person able to do many different things.
Choose the sentence in which "meticulous" is used correctly. In each option, the clause after "because" gives the sole stated reason for describing the clerk as meticulous.
In each sentence, the clause after “because” gives the reason for describing the person as resilient. Choose the sentence in which “resilient” is used correctly.

Choose the word that best completes the sentence. Although the panel had explained both proposals, Meera showed no interest in either one and did not care which was selected; she was ____ about the choice.
Choose the sentence in which "prudent" is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which "gregarious" is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which “discreet” is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which "sparse" is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which “transient” describes something that continues for only a short time.
Choose the sentence in which "reluctant" is used correctly. In each sentence, the stated circumstance is the sole explanation for using the word.

At a project meeting, Rohan presented a proposal confirmed to be his genuine, original work. While discussing it, he treated his judgement as superior to everyone else’s and dismissed the effects of his decision on colleagues as unimportant. He remained friendly, did not seek an argument or fight, and was not watching for signs of danger or trouble. Which word best describes his manner toward his colleagues?

Lena said that a service suspension on her train caused her to miss a meeting. An independently checked station record confirms that the train was suspended at the time she stated, and the passenger register confirms that she was on it. Which word best describes her explanation?

An official states that a storm will miss the city. A journalist doubts that the statement is true and asks for evidence before accepting it. Which word best describes the journalist’s attitude towards the statement?
The dictionary defines "authentic" as “known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy.” Choose the sentence in which "authentic" is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which "obsolete" is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which "elated" is used correctly.
Choose the sentence in which “arrogant” is used correctly. In each option, the stated details are the complete context for the description.
The supplied dictionary sense of "plausible" is “(of an excuse or explanation) reasonable and likely to be true”. Choose the sentence in which "plausible" is used in this sense.
Choose the sentence in which "diligent" is used correctly.

A field team compares the work involved in four assignments. In each option, the details given are the complete context for judging the description. Choose the sentence in which "arduous" is used correctly.

Choose the sentence in which "arrogant" is used correctly. In each sentence, the stated behaviour is the only basis for the description.

Mira expected the project to succeed and encouraged her colleagues, showing no sense of superiority or disregard for them; the report called her arrogant.
At the residents’ meeting, Dev dismissed neighbours’ concerns as unimportant and spoke as if only his judgement mattered; the report called him arrogant.
Ravi treated colleagues as equals and considered their concerns, but became aggressive and ready to fight; the report called him arrogant.
Sana showed no interest in which plan was chosen while treating everyone respectfully; the report called her arrogant.

Choose the sentence in which "diligent" is used correctly. Here, diligent means showing care and effort in one's work or duties. In each sentence, the stated conduct is the sole basis for describing Nila as diligent.
Choose the sentence in which “hostile” is used correctly. In each sentence, the stated behaviour or reason is the sole basis for using the word.

ideas.body:
A partnership’s Profit and Loss Account has a credit balance representing net profit, and interest on capital is to be allowed. Arrange the following journal-entry steps in the order used to prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account:
(A) Allow interest on capital: debit Interest on Capital A/c and credit the partners’ Capital/Current A/cs.
(B) Transfer net profit: debit Profit and Loss A/c and credit Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c.
(C) Transfer interest on capital: debit Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c and credit Interest on Capital A/c.
Choose the correct sequence.
A partnership firm has no specific agreement among its partners about the distribution of profits. Which rule governs this issue?

Assume a partnership deed provides for interest on capital, but it is omitted from the accounts. The final accounts are prepared and profit is distributed before the omission is discovered. Arrange the following stages of the past adjustment in the correct order:
(A) Make the correction through the Profit and Loss Adjustment Account or directly in the concerned partners’ capital accounts, without altering the old accounts.
(B) Prepare the final accounts and distribute the profit.
(C) Calculate the omitted interest and determine its effect on the distribution already made.
(D) Discover the omission.
Choose the correct sequence.
Partners have no specific agreement on a matter affecting the distribution of profits. Which provisions apply in this situation?

Four stages in a partnership are described below. The partners first reach an agreement orally on business terms. They then record those agreed terms in a written document. At a later stage, they decide to change one clause in that document; all partners give consent before the clause is changed. Arrange the listed events in the order they occur.
(A) All partners consent to the proposed clause change.
(B) The written document containing the agreed terms is identified as the Partnership Deed.
(C) The partners reach the agreement on the business terms.
(D) The clause is changed.
Choose the correct sequence.

A sole-proprietary business is expanding and now needs more capital, a larger number of people to manage it, and a way to share its business risks. Which organisational form is usually adopted in this situation?

A firm maintains partners’ accounts under the fixed capital method. During the year, partner R is allocated a share of profit and makes ordinary drawings. No additional capital is introduced, and no part of R’s capital is withdrawn under the partnership agreement. What happens to R’s Capital Account during the year?
Leena and Farah agree orally to enter into a partnership. They have not prepared a written document. Which statement correctly describes whether their agreement must be in writing?

The firm decides to correct the omission without altering the old accounts and chooses the direct method rather than a Profit and Loss Adjustment Account. Where should it make the adjustment?

Match each transaction in List-I with the corresponding journal entry in List-II. In each entry, the account before “To” is debited and the account after “To” is credited. For (A), the Profit and Loss A/c has a credit balance (net profit).
List-I
(A) Transfer of net profit from the Profit and Loss A/c
(B) Allowing interest on capital
(C) Charging interest on drawings to partners’ capital/current accounts
(D) Transfer of interest on drawings to the Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c
List-II
(I) Interest on Drawings A/c Dr.; To Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c
(II) Profit and Loss A/c Dr.; To Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c
(III) Partners’ Capital/Current A/cs (individually) Dr.; To Interest on Drawings A/c
(IV) Interest on Capital A/c Dr.; To Partners’ Capital/Current A/cs (individually)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A partnership firm's Profit and Loss A/c has a debit balance of ₹18,000, representing the entire net loss for the year. The entry requested is only the transfer of that balance to the Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c, before any loss is allocated to partners. Which journal entry records this transfer?

A firm has prepared its Profit and Loss A/c, which shows a net profit. Its partnership terms provide for a partner’s salary and interest on capital, and the firm needs to record these adjustments and show how the profit is appropriated among the partners. Which account should it use?

A partnership has a profit remaining after all appropriations, which is to be distributed among its partners. It maintains a separate current account for each partner. Only the distribution of this remaining profit is being recorded. Which journal entry records the distribution?

P and Q share profits in the ratio 3:2. For a year, Q’s share calculated on that basis is below Q’s guaranteed minimum profit. P is the only partner who has given the guarantee. Who bears the deficiency?

A partner advances ₹1,20,000 to a firm for business use. The loan remains outstanding for six months without repayment. The partnership deed is silent on interest on the loan. Apply the annual rate proportionately for six months. Consider the following statements:
(A) No interest is payable because the deed is silent.
(B) Interest payable for six months is ₹3,600.
(C) The applicable annual rate is 6%.
(D) Interest payable for six months is ₹7,200.

A firm’s existing partners change their profit-sharing ratio without admitting or retiring a partner. The firm undertakes revaluation of its assets and reassessment of its liabilities. Arrange the following steps in the order in which the revaluation adjustment is completed:
(A) Transfer the final balance of the Revaluation Account to the old partners’ capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio.
(B) Identify assets and liabilities requiring value changes, including any unrecorded items.
(C) Record revaluation gains and losses in the Revaluation Account.
(D) Determine whether the Revaluation Account has a credit or debit balance.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

P and Q continue as partners in a firm, with no admission or retirement. They revise their profit-sharing ratio, under which P sacrifices a share and Q gains a share. A goodwill adjustment is required. Which treatment correctly records this adjustment?

Partners P, Q, R and S change their profit-sharing ratio from 5:4:2:1 to 3:5:1:3, respectively. There is no admission or retirement of a partner. Match each partner with the change in that partner’s share.
List-I
(A) Partner P
(B) Partner Q
(C) Partner R
(D) Partner S
List-II
(I) Sacrifices 1/12
(II) Gains 1/12
(III) Sacrifices 1/6
(IV) Gains 1/6
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A, B and C continue as partners without any admission or retirement. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2, and their new ratio is 4:2:4. The total goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹90,000 and is to be adjusted through the partners’ capital accounts. For this question, the amount transferred for goodwill is the total goodwill multiplied by the fraction of profit transferred. Credit the sacrificing partners in proportion to their sacrifices and debit the gaining partners in proportion to their gains. Which adjustment is correct?

A, B, C and D continue as partners; no partner is admitted or retires. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2:2, and their agreed new ratio is 7:5:4:2. The firm has goodwill, and its value is to be adjusted for the change in ratio. Which treatment correctly identifies the sacrificing and gaining partners and records the goodwill adjustment?

P, Q and R are existing partners sharing future profits in the ratio 5:3:2. Without admitting or retiring any partner, they change the ratio to 4:4:2. Treat each partner’s share as that partner’s ratio parts divided by the total ratio parts. Which set correctly gives their shares after the change?

Three existing partners A, B and C share profits in the old ratio 7:5:3 and agree to a new ratio 5:6:4. These are complete ratios for the same three partners; no partner is admitted or retires. An increase in a partner’s fractional share is a gain, and a decrease is a sacrifice.
(A) A sacrifices 2/15 of the profit share.
(B) B gains 1/15 of the profit share.
(C) C gains 1/15 of the profit share.
(D) A gains 2/15 of the profit share.
Which statements are correct?

A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. C is admitted for a 1/5 share. No separate arrangement is made for how C acquires this share; assume C acquires it from A and B in their old profit-sharing ratio. What is the new profit-sharing ratio A:B:C?

ideas.body:
Consider the following statements about goodwill under the Average Profits Method:
(A) Goodwill is calculated by multiplying average past profits by the agreed number of years’ purchase.
(B) Goodwill is calculated by dividing average past profits by the agreed number of years’ purchase.
(C) The method is based on the assumption that a new business will not be able to earn profits during its first few years of operations.
(D) This method always gives the same goodwill value as every other method.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

A firm values goodwill using the Average Profits Method. Its profits for the three past years were ₹36,000, ₹48,000 and ₹60,000. Calculate average past profit as the arithmetic mean of these three profits, and use an agreed three years’ purchase. What is the goodwill value?

P and Q are existing partners sharing profits in the old ratio of 3:2. Without admitting or retiring a partner, they change their ratio to 2:3. The firm has goodwill, and the partners decide to adjust it. Consider the following statements:
(A) P’s share falls from 3/5 to 2/5, so P sacrifices a share.
(B) Q’s share rises from 2/5 to 3/5, so Q gains a share.
(C) The goodwill adjustment should debit P and credit Q.
(D) The goodwill adjustment should credit P and debit Q.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

P and Q are existing partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. R is admitted, and the terms state that R’s share will come from the existing partners but do not specify how it is to be acquired. Under the stated assumption for an unspecified acquisition, in what ratio do P and Q sacrifice their shares?

A, B and C are existing partners; no partner is admitted or retires. Their complete old and revised profit-sharing ratios are 6:3:1 and 4:4:2, respectively. Firm goodwill is valued at ₹1,20,000. Goodwill is adjusted through partners’ capital accounts; calculate each partner’s amount using firm goodwill multiplied by that partner’s gain or sacrifice in share. What amount is debited to B’s capital account?

Match each case’s stated average past profit and agreed years’ purchase with its goodwill value under the Average Profits Method. No adjustments apply.
List-I
(A) ₹18,000; 4 years
(B) ₹25,000; 3 years
(C) ₹32,000; 2 years
(D) ₹28,000; 5 years
List-II
(I) ₹64,000
(II) ₹1,40,000
(III) ₹75,000
(IV) ₹72,000
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

To estimate a deceased partner’s share of profit for the period from the last balance sheet to death, a firm uses the preceding year’s profit as its base. Arrange the steps in the correct order.
(A) Record the firm’s profit for the preceding year as the base.
(B) Next, apply the fraction of a year elapsed from the last balance sheet to the date of death.
(C) Then apply the deceased partner’s profit-sharing fraction to the time-apportioned profit.
(D) Finally, treat the result as the estimated share for the intervening period.

A partner retires on 30 September. His capital remained ₹4,80,000 from 1 April through 30 September. Interest on capital applies at 10% per annum, calculated as simple interest pro rata for this six-month period, and is unpaid. What amount of interest on capital is included in the amount due to him?

ideas.body:
In a partnership firm, consider the following statements about choosing a method to value goodwill:
(A) The existing partners and the incoming partner cannot specifically decide the method.
(B) The existing partners and the incoming partner may specifically decide the method.
(C) The incoming partner alone may decide the method.
(D) The existing partners alone may decide the method.
Which statement is correct?

At the admission of a partner, a firm undertakes the following revaluation-related steps. Arrange them in the correct procedural order.
(A) Transfer the final balance of the Revaluation Account to the old partners’ capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio.
(B) Check whether the recorded assets are shown at their current values.
(C) Revalue overstated or understated assets, reassess liabilities, and bring any unrecorded assets and liabilities into the books.
(D) Prepare the Revaluation Account.
(E) Record gains or losses from the asset and liability adjustments, and the entries for unrecorded items, in the Revaluation Account.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

At the admission of a partner, arrange the following steps in the order described for revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities.
(A) Transfer the balance of the Revaluation Account to the old partners’ capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio.
(B) Prepare the Revaluation Account.
(C) Ascertain whether assets are shown at current values and reassess liabilities to their correct values.
(D) Transfer the gain or loss on revaluation of each asset and liability to the Revaluation Account.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

P and Q are the only existing partners and share profits in the ratio 3:2. R is admitted for 1/5 of the profits. No specific arrangement is made about how R acquires this share, so assume it is acquired from P and Q in their old profit-sharing ratio.

Arrange the following steps to determine the new profit-sharing ratio:
(A) Deduct the allocated sacrifices from P’s and Q’s old shares.
(B) Record the resulting shares of P, Q and R as 12/25, 8/25 and 1/5, respectively.
(C) Apportion R’s 1/5 share between P and Q in their old 3:2 ratio.
(D) Calculate P’s and Q’s respective sacrifices from R’s share as 3/25 and 2/25.

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

A, B and C share profits in the ratio 4:3:2. N is admitted and receives a 1/5 share in the profits. The partners agree that N acquires this entire share from A, B and C in the ratio 2:1:1, respectively. This ratio specifies the proportions of N’s share contributed by A, B and C. What is the new profit-sharing ratio of A, B, C and N?

On admission of a new partner, the old and new profit shares of the four existing partners are given below. Each fraction is a share of the firm’s total profit; the incoming partner receives the residual share.
List-I
(A) P: old share 1/2; new share 2/5
(B) Q: old share 1/4; new share 1/5
(C) R: old share 1/6; new share 2/15
(D) S: old share 1/12; new share 1/15
List-II
(I) 1/20
(II) 1/60
(III) 1/10
(IV) 1/30
Match List-I with List-II to identify each existing partner’s sacrifice of profit share. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A new partner brings a goodwill premium of ₹1,20,000 through the firm. The firm credits the premium to the new partner’s capital account and then adjusts it in favour of the two sacrificing partners, A and B, in their sacrifice ratio of 3:2. A and B each withdraw one-quarter of the amount credited to their respective capital accounts. No other adjustment affects A’s capital account. What amount of this premium remains credited to A’s capital account after the withdrawal?

A firm admits T. Before admission, P, Q, R and S have profit shares of 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/8, respectively. After admission, their respective profit shares are P 1/3, Q 1/8, R 1/24 and S 1/12; T’s share is 5/12. Match each old partner with that partner’s individual sacrifice in profit share.

List-I
(A) P: old share 1/2; new share 1/3
(B) Q: old share 1/4; new share 1/8
(C) R: old share 1/8; new share 1/24
(D) S: old share 1/8; new share 1/12

List-II
(I) 1/24
(II) 1/12
(III) 1/8
(IV) 1/6

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

At the admission of T, X and Y are the existing partners, sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. The agreed profit-sharing ratio after T’s admission is X:Y:T = 4:3:3. The firm has an untransferred reserve of ₹24,000, a general reserve of ₹18,000 and a credit balance of ₹33,000 in the Profit and Loss Account. All three balances are accumulated profits from before T’s admission. What amounts should be allocated to X, Y and T, respectively, from these accumulated profits?

A new partner brings the agreed goodwill premium in cash through the firm. The firm credits the premium to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio. The partners decide to retain the credited amount in the business. Which treatment is required for this decision?

A new partner pays a cash premium for goodwill directly to the existing partners, privately. The firm does not receive or record the payment. What should the firm record in its books for this payment?

At T’s admission, the firm has an untransferred General Reserve of ₹1,00,000. M and N are the existing partners and share profits in the old ratio 3:2. Assume this is the only accumulated profit being adjusted.
Which statements are correct?
(A) T receives a share of the reserve according to the new ratio.
(B) The reserve is distributed between M and N in their old ratio.
(C) ₹60,000 is transferred to M’s and ₹40,000 to N’s capital/current account.
(D) The reserve is distributed among all partners according to the new ratio.

A and B have an old profit-sharing ratio of 3:2. When N is admitted, the new ratio among A, B and N is 2:2:1. A general reserve is an accumulated profit not yet transferred to the partners’ accounts. Which treatment is appropriate?

Match each case with the amount credited to P’s capital account. P and Q are the existing partners. In each case, the new partner brings the stated premium in cash through the firm, and the full premium is credited to P’s and Q’s capital accounts in their sacrifice ratio. No amount is withdrawn or otherwise adjusted. Each stated ratio is P:Q’s sacrifice ratio.
List-I
(A) ₹1,44,000; 5:3
(B) ₹1,65,000; 7:4
(C) ₹1,82,000; 6:7
(D) ₹1,44,000; 5:4
List-II
(I) ₹90,000
(II) ₹1,05,000
(III) ₹84,000
(IV) ₹80,000
