ideas.body:
Consider the following statements about the amount due to a deceased partner:
(A) The partner’s share of accumulated profits is included in the amount due.
(B) Interest on capital, if applicable, up to the date of death is included in the amount due.
(C) Interest on drawings, if applicable, up to the date of death is deducted from the partner’s share.
(D) The partner’s share of a loss on revaluation is added to the amount due.
Which of the statements are correct?

Assume all four items below apply and are attributable to the deceased partner. Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Deceased partner’s share of accumulated profits (reserves)
(B) Deceased partner’s share of accumulated losses
(C) Interest on the deceased partner’s capital up to the date of death
(D) Interest on the deceased partner’s drawings up to the date of death

List-II
(I) Included in the deceased partner’s claim as a share of accumulated profits
(II) Deducted from the deceased partner’s claim as a share of accumulated losses
(III) Included in the deceased partner’s claim as interest on capital
(IV) Deducted from the deceased partner’s claim as interest on drawings

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A deceased partner’s executor’s claim is being calculated. All amounts below are in rupees, represent the deceased partner’s amount or share where applicable, and are unpaid. All listed items apply, and no other items, payments or set-offs affect the claim.

Credit balance of capital account: ₹1,00,000
Credit balance of current account: ₹8,000
Share of goodwill: ₹15,000
Share of accumulated profits: ₹12,000
Share of gain on revaluation: ₹5,000
Share of profit up to the date of death: ₹9,000
Interest on capital up to the date of death: ₹4,000
Salary due up to the date of death: ₹3,000
Share of accumulated losses: ₹6,000
Drawings up to the date of death: ₹7,000
Interest on drawings up to the date of death: ₹1,000

What amount is due to the deceased partner’s executor?

A firm is calculating the amount due to the executor of a deceased partner. All amounts below are already the deceased partner’s attributable amounts, in rupees, and the partner has not yet been paid. The partner’s capital account has a credit balance of ₹1,50,000 and the current account has a credit balance of ₹8,000. The partner’s share of goodwill is ₹25,000, accumulated profits are ₹12,000, and the gain on revaluation is ₹5,000. The partner’s share of profit up to death is ₹15,000; interest on capital due up to death is ₹3,000; and salary due up to death is ₹2,000. The partner’s share of accumulated losses is ₹6,000, and drawings to be deducted are ₹9,000. There are no other credits or deductions. What amount is due to the executor?

A deceased partner’s claim is being calculated at the date of death. The following amounts are separate, apply to the deceased partner, and have not been adjusted against one another:
Credit balance of capital account: ₹1,20,000
Share of profit up to the date of death: ₹12,000
Interest on capital up to the date of death: ₹4,000
Salary due up to the date of death: ₹6,000
Share of accumulated losses: ₹5,000
Drawings up to the date of death: ₹7,000
Interest on drawings up to the date of death: ₹1,000
Share of loss on revaluation: ₹3,000
No other amount is due or deductible. What is the amount of the deceased partner’s claim before settlement with the executor?

A deceased partner’s claim is being prepared. Assume all applicable credit items and deductions have already been identified and their amounts are known. No other adjustments or payments affect the claim. Arrange the following stages in the order needed to determine and deal with the amount due.

(A) Add the applicable credit items to obtain the gross claim.
(B) Subtract the applicable deductions from the gross claim to obtain the net amount due.
(C) Transfer the resulting claim to the deceased partner’s executors.
(D) Settle the executors’ claim in the same manner as a retired partner’s claim.

Choose the correct sequence:

On 31 October 2025, the last balance sheet of a firm was prepared. A partner, entitled to 1/4 of the firm’s profits, died on 31 March 2026. The firm’s profits for the three preceding years were ₹2,40,000, ₹3,00,000 and ₹3,60,000. For this estimate, the firm uses the average of those three annual profits and assumes profit accrues evenly over the 12-month year. What is the deceased partner’s estimated share of profit for the five-month period from 1 November 2025 to 31 March 2026?

At the firm’s last balance sheet date, 31 March 20X5, partner R died on 31 August 20X5. The firm’s profits for the three completed years immediately preceding 31 March 20X5 were ₹2,10,000, ₹2,40,000 and ₹2,70,000. The partners shared profits in the ratio 3:5:2, and R’s share remained 3 parts throughout the relevant period. The firm estimates the profit for the intervening period using the arithmetic average of these three annual profits, apportioned evenly over 12 months. The period from 1 April to 31 August is treated as five complete months. What amount of profit should be included in the amount due to R’s executor for this period?

A partner retires on 30 September. The firm’s accounting year is 1 April to 31 March, and interest on the partner’s capital applies and accrues from 1 April. How many months of interest on capital are included in the amount due to the partner at retirement?

A firm’s last Balance Sheet was prepared on 31 March. A partner whose share of profits was 3/10 died on 31 August. The preceding year’s profit was ₹2,40,000. Using that profit as the base and five-twelfths as the proportionate period, what is the deceased partner’s estimated share of profit for the intervening period?

ideas.body: On dissolution, all the firm’s assets have been realised in cash for ₹6,70,000. The firm owes ₹3,20,000 to outside creditors. After those creditors are paid, the only partner advances due are loans of ₹1,20,000 to P and ₹80,000 to Q. Capital claims are ₹1,20,000 for P and ₹1,80,000 for Q, and P and Q share profits equally. There are no other liabilities, realisation expenses, assets, or partner contributions. How much should P receive in total against the partner loan and capital?
Which statement correctly describes the relationship between dissolution of a firm and dissolution of the partnership?

After all dissolution transactions have been posted, the Realisation A/c of a firm shows a final credit balance of ₹24,000. Which journal entry transfers this profit to the partners’ individual accounts?

At the start of a year, A and B carry on a business as a firm. On 1 April, C is admitted and the business continues without the firm closing. On 1 October, B retires and A and C continue the same business; the firm remains open. No assets are realised, liabilities settled or books closed on either date. On 31 March, A and C discontinue the business altogether, realise all the firm’s assets, pay all its liabilities, settle the accounts and close the books. Which option correctly classifies the admission, retirement and final closure?

A firm is being dissolved. Its firm liabilities exceed its firm assets. Partner R has private debts and private property. Which statement correctly describes the application of R’s private property under the settlement rules?

A partnership is constituted for a fixed term ending on 30 June. Its business remains unfinished on that date. No contract extends the term or provides otherwise. What is the status of the firm when the fixed term expires?

At dissolution, non-cash assets have a book value of ₹6,40,000 and are sold for ₹5,50,000. External liabilities have a book value of ₹2,00,000 and are settled for ₹1,82,000. Realisation expenses of ₹12,000 are paid in cash. For this question, debit the Realisation Account with the book value of assets, the cash paid to settle liabilities and realisation expenses; credit it with the book value of external liabilities and the proceeds from the sale of assets. These are the only items affecting the account. What is its resulting balance?

During dissolution, a previously unrecorded liability of ₹12,000 is fully settled by payment from the firm’s bank. Consider the following statements about the entry for this transaction.
(A) Realisation A/c is debited by ₹12,000.
(B) Bank A/c is credited by ₹12,000.
(C) Bank A/c is debited by ₹12,000.
(D) Partners’ Capital A/cs are credited by ₹12,000.
Select the correct statements.

A firm has ₹3,60,000 available from assets realised and owes ₹4,00,000 to creditors. Its only partners, A and B, share profits in the ratio 3:2. There are no other funds or payments to consider. Creditors are paid first from realised assets, and any shortfall is met by partner contributions in the profit-sharing ratio. How much must B contribute?

On dissolution, a firm has ₹2,00,000 available from realised assets. It first pays outside liabilities of ₹80,000. The only claims remaining before capital settlement are partner advances: P is due ₹90,000 and Q ₹60,000. The balance is insufficient to repay them fully. P and Q share profits in the ratio 4:1; no other payments or contributions are involved. How much does P receive towards the advance?

ideas.body:
A company receives applications for more shares than it offered. Match each description of the directors’ approach or the accounting perspective with the corresponding statement.

List-I
(A) Some applications are accepted in full and the others are rejected
(B) A pro-rata allotment is made to all applicants
(C) The directors combine the two approaches described in (A) and (B)
(D) Accounting perspective on when and within which process over-subscription is resolved

List-II
(I) Shares are allotted to all applicants proportionately
(II) Full acceptance and rejection are used together with pro-rata allotment
(III) It is resolved with allotment and considered within the application-and-allotment process
(IV) Selected applications are accepted in full, and the others are rejected

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company purchases a business from a vendor and settles the entire purchase price by issuing fully paid shares to that vendor. No cash is paid to the vendor. In the same period, the company receives application money in cash from public applicants for a separate share issue. How should the shares issued to the vendor be classified?

At the reporting date, a company has received ₹4,80,000 as calls in advance. Before that date, ₹1,80,000 of this amount was adjusted when the related call became due. The company also received a further ₹90,000 in advance for a call not yet due. No other receipts or adjustments affect the Calls in Advance Account. What balance should be shown under current liabilities as Calls in Advance?

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Authorised capital
(B) Issued capital
(C) Subscribed capital
(D) Called-up capital

List-II
(I) The amount of share capital a company is authorised to issue by its Memorandum of Association
(II) The part of authorised capital actually issued to the public for subscription, including shares allotted to vendors and signatories to the company’s memorandum
(III) The part of issued capital actually subscribed by the public
(IV) The part of subscribed capital called up by the company for payment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Consider the following statements about collecting the amount on shares:
(A) The first instalment collected with the application is called application money.
(B) The second instalment, collected on allotment, is called allotment money.
(C) Any remaining instalments are termed calls on shares.
(D) A company is required to collect the amount on shares in at least three instalments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company has ₹2,00,000 of uncalled capital, of which ₹50,000 is designated as Reserve Capital. The company is not being wound up and needs funds for its normal operations. Which statement applies to the ₹50,000?

A company receives cash from shareholders towards a call that has not yet been made. The amount is specifically paid in advance and is not currently due. Which statements are correct?

(I) The amount received is called Calls in Advance.
(II) The amount is a liability of the company.
(III) The amount is credited directly to Share Capital Account upon receipt.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Share
(B) Company
(C) Stages for issue of shares for cash
(D) Issue of shares for consideration other than cash

List-II
(I) Application, allotment and call/calls
(II) Fractional part of capital and basis of ownership
(III) Shares given fully paid to vendors who accept them as payment when a company purchases a business or asset(s)
(IV) Organisation of shareholders that can act as a legal person in its business through a board of directors

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company validly forfeits shares issued at a premium after a shareholder fails to pay a call. The full share premium had already been received and recorded before forfeiture, and no share premium is outstanding. What is the treatment of the recorded share-premium entry?

A company has received an amount from a shareholder before the relevant call is made. The amount remains unadjusted until that call becomes due. Match each event or question in List-I with the corresponding treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) Receipt of the amount before the call is made
(B) Adjustment of the advance when the relevant call becomes due
(C) Balance-sheet presentation of the unadjusted amount
(D) Treatment of the amount in determining paid-up capital

List-II
(I) Show separately under Equity and Liabilities, under current liabilities, as ‘others current liabilities’
(II) Debit Bank A/c and credit Calls in Advance A/c
(III) Do not add the amount to paid-up capital
(IV) Debit Calls in Advance A/c and credit the Particular Call A/c

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company forfeits 100 shares of ₹10 each, issued at par. The full ₹10 per share has been called up. Each shareholder paid ₹3 per share on application but did not pay the ₹2 per share allotment money or the ₹5 per share call money. No other amount is unpaid.

Match each account and entry direction in List-I with the amount to be recorded in the forfeiture entry in List-II.

List-I
(A) Share Capital A/c (Dr.)
(B) Share Forfeiture A/c (Cr.)
(C) Share Allotment A/c (Cr.)
(D) Share Calls A/c (Cr.)

List-II
(I) ₹1,000
(II) ₹300
(III) ₹200
(IV) ₹500

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company issues shares for cash and collects the amount in four separate instalments: application money, allotment money, a first call and a final call. The calls are made successively, with the first call preceding the final call. Arrange the instalments in chronological order.
(A) Application money
(B) Allotment money
(C) First call money
(D) Final call money
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company has 24,000 allotted shares, and the second and final call of ₹18 per share is due on every share. Calls in advance of ₹72,000 have already been received and are available in full to adjust against this call. The remaining call money is received in full in cash on the due date, with no other receipts or deductions. How much cash does the company receive on the due date?

A company has received ₹2,40,000 as calls in advance. Subsequently, calls of ₹80,000 and ₹95,000 become due, and the full amount of each call is adjusted against the advance. No other advance is received or adjusted. What is the balance in Calls in Advance Account immediately after these adjustments? Ignore interest.

A company has forfeited 500 shares. It subsequently reissues 200 of those shares, while the other 300 remain unreissued. Consider the following statements about the reissue:
(A) Capital profit transferred to Capital Reserve can relate only to the shares reissued.
(B) Any discount allowed on reissue is debited to Share Forfeiture Account.
(C) The entire balance of Share Forfeiture Account for all 500 shares may be transferred to Capital Reserve after only 200 shares are reissued.
(D) Forfeited shares may be reissued only at par.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company receives calls in advance from shareholders. Match each situation in List-I with the accounting treatment in List-II. Assume no other transaction affects these balances.

List-I
(A) A shareholder pays an amount before the related call is due.
(B) The related call becomes due, and the available advance is adjusted against it.
(C) At the balance-sheet date, the related call is not yet due and the advance remains unadjusted.
(D) Interest on the advance is paid through the bank; assume the Articles provide for this interest.

List-II
(I) Calls in Advance A/c Dr.; To Particular Call A/c.
(II) Show the balance separately under current liabilities—other current liabilities; exclude it from paid-up capital.
(III) Bank A/c Dr.; To Calls in Advance A/c.
(IV) Interest on Calls in Advance A/c Dr.; To Bank A/c.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Arrange the following statements in logical order, beginning with why a company obtains capital from several persons and ending with how their contributions are represented in its accounts.
(A) The contributions are combined in a common account called Share Capital Account.
(B) Since it cannot generate its own capital, the company obtains capital from several persons.
(C) The contributors are shareholders, and their contributions are share capital.
(D) Because shareholders are numerous, a separate capital account is not opened for each.
Choose the correct sequence.

A company collects capital from a very large number of persons. No separate capital account is opened for each person; their contributions are combined in one common capital account. Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) The persons contributing capital
(B) The amount contributed by those persons
(C) The common account in which the contributions are combined
(D) The stated reason for not opening a separate capital account for each person

List-II
(I) Share Capital Account
(II) Shareholders
(III) Share capital
(IV) The very large number of shareholders

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company issued shares at a premium. Before the shares were validly forfeited for non-payment of a call, the entire premium due on them had been received and recorded. What should be done with the recorded share-premium entry when the shares are forfeited?

A company issued shares at a premium. The entire premium was received and credited to Share Premium A/c before the shares were forfeited for non-payment of a call. What should be done with the entry recording the premium already received?

A company offers 70,000 shares of face value ₹10 each for subscription. Applications are received for 63,000 shares, and all 63,000 shares are allotted. The company calls ₹8 per allotted share. Holders of 3,000 allotted shares do not pay any amount called; all other allottees pay ₹8 per share.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Issued capital
(B) Subscribed capital
(C) Called-up capital
(D) Paid-up capital

List-II
(I) ₹4,80,000
(II) ₹7,00,000
(III) ₹5,04,000
(IV) ₹6,30,000

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A company has forfeited shares with a face value of ₹10 each. The directors propose to reissue them as fully paid for ₹12 per share. Which description of the proposed reissue is correct?

A company has three groups of shareholders: 120 shareholders each contribute ₹2,500, 80 each contribute ₹3,750 and 50 each contribute ₹4,000. These are the only contributions towards its share capital. What is the total share capital represented by these contributions?

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Company
(B) Share
(C) Issue of shares for cash
(D) Issue of shares for consideration other than cash

List-II
(I) Fractional part of capital forming the basis of ownership
(II) Shareholders’ organisation acting as a legal person through a board of directors
(III) Amount collected at application, allotment or calls
(IV) Fully paid shares accepted by a vendor for a business or asset

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A company has subscribed share capital of ₹10,00,000. It has called up ₹7,00,000 on these shares, and the remaining ₹3,00,000 has not been called. How is the remaining amount classified?

A company offers 24,000 shares and receives valid applications for 36,000 shares. The directors make a pro-rata allotment to all applicants. An applicant has applied for 900 shares. Assuming the pro-rata ratio is applied uniformly, how many shares are allotted to this applicant?

Two batches of shares are forfeited. Each share in both batches has a face value of ₹10 and was issued at par. In Batch I, 240 shares have ₹10 per share called up; ₹7 per share has been paid and ₹3 per share remains unpaid. In Batch II, 160 shares have ₹8 per share called up; ₹5 per share has been paid and ₹3 per share remains unpaid. No premium is involved, and these are the only shares forfeited. What total amount is credited to Share Forfeiture A/c?

A company has authorised capital of 1,00,000 shares. It issues 65,000 shares to the public for subscription and allots 10,000 shares to vendors and signatories to its memorandum. No other shares have been issued or offered for subscription. Which term specifically classifies the remaining 25,000 authorised shares that have not been offered for subscription, rather than the company’s total authorised amount?

Shares issued at par are forfeited for non-payment of allotment money and calls; application money has been paid. Arrange the following account entries in the order in which they appear in the forfeiture journal entry.
(A) Credit Share Allotment A/c for the unpaid allotment amount
(B) Debit Share Capital A/c for the called-up amount
(C) Credit Share Forfeiture A/c for the paid-up amount
(D) Credit Share Calls A/c(s) for the unpaid call amount

A company offers 10,000 shares and receives valid applications for 15,000 shares. The directors allot 3,000 shares in full to applicants for 3,000 shares, reject applications for 2,000 shares, and allot the remaining 7,000 shares pro rata among applicants for 10,000 shares. These three groups are distinct and together account for all applications. Which policy describes this allotment?

A company offers 12,000 shares and receives applications for 15,000 shares, one share per application. The shares are issued at par; application money is received for all applications, 3,000 applications are rejected and fully refunded, and the allotment amount on 12,000 shares is later called and fully received. Match each transaction in List-I with its journal entry in List-II.
List-I
(A) Receipt of application money
(B) Transfer of application money for shares allotted and refund for rejected applications
(C) Amount due on allotment
(D) Receipt of allotment money
List-II
(I) Bank A/c Dr; To Share Application A/c
(II) Share Application A/c Dr; To Share Capital A/c; To Bank A/c
(III) Share Allotment A/c Dr; To Share Capital A/c
(IV) Bank A/c Dr; To Share Allotment A/c
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company forfeited 100 shares on identical terms. Forty have been reissued and the remaining 60 have not. The Share Forfeiture Account balance attributable to the reissued and unreissued shares is separately identifiable. Which portion of the balance may be transferred to Capital Reserve as capital profit?

A company issued 400 shares of ₹10 each at par. It called up ₹8 per share. The holders paid ₹5 per share, leaving ₹3 per share unpaid, and the company forfeited all 400 shares. No premium was involved. What amount is credited to Share Forfeiture A/c in the forfeiture entry?

ideas.body: A company issues debentures with a nominal value of ₹100 each for ₹110 each. Considering only the premium on issue, which account is credited with the ₹10 premium per debenture?

A company issues 800 debentures of nominal value ₹100 each for ₹112 each, 500 debentures of nominal value ₹200 each for ₹218 each, and 300 debentures of nominal value ₹500 each for ₹506 each. All the debentures are issued for the stated prices, and there are no other adjustments. Which option correctly states the total premium on issue and its balance sheet presentation?

A company issues debentures with a nominal value of ₹1,000 each, receives ₹900 per debenture at issue, and undertakes to repay ₹1,100 per debenture on maturity. For this question, an issue proceeds amount below nominal value is an issue at a discount, and a repayment amount above nominal value is redemption at a premium.

(A) The debentures are issued at a discount and redeemable at a premium.
(B) Issue at a discount and redemption at a premium is one of the six situations commonly found in practice.
(C) Because the debentures are issued at a discount, they must be redeemed at par.
(D) Because the debentures are redeemable at a premium, they must have been issued at a premium.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

A company issues 500 debentures, each having a nominal value of ₹320, at an issue price of ₹400 per debenture. All 500 debentures are issued at that price. Calculate the premium as a percentage of the total nominal value, using (total premium ÷ total nominal value) × 100. What is the premium percentage?
(A) 25%
(B) 20%
(C) 125%
(D) 80%

Each amount below is per debenture. Which statements are correct?
(A) A debenture with a nominal value of ₹500 issued for ₹540 carries an issue premium of ₹40.
(B) A debenture with a nominal value of ₹500 issued for ₹500 carries an issue premium of ₹500.
(C) A debenture with a nominal value of ₹500 issued for ₹460 carries an issue premium of ₹40.
(D) On an issue at a premium, the premium is credited to Securities Premium Reserve and shown on the liabilities side under “Reserves and Surpluses”.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company issues two debenture series, each with a nominal value of ₹1,000. Series X is issued for ₹1,080 and repaid at maturity for ₹1,120; Series Y is issued for ₹940 and repaid at maturity for ₹1,000. For both issue price and maturity repayment, an amount equal to nominal value is at par and an amount above it is at a premium; an issue price below nominal value is at a discount. Which option correctly classifies both series?

Match each case to its entry. A–C: allotment; D: application-money receipt. Assume no adjustments.
List-I
(A) Par issue, par redemption; allotment
(B) Discount issue, par redemption; allotment
(C) Premium issue, par redemption; allotment
(D) Par issue, par redemption; application-money receipt
List-II
(I) Bank Dr; Debenture Application & Allotment Cr
(II) Debenture Application & Allotment Dr; Debentures Cr
(III) Debenture Application & Allotment and Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr; Debentures Cr
(IV) Debenture Application & Allotment Dr; Debentures and Securities Premium Reserve Cr
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company issues 240 debentures at the same price. The total amount charged is ₹3,24,000, and the issue price per debenture is ₹150 more than its nominal value. What is the nominal value of each debenture?

ideas.body: A company issues balance sheets dated 31 March and 30 September. A manager uses the 31 March balance sheet to describe the company’s position at both dates. Which interpretation is supported?

A shareholder and an external party use a business concern's financial statements when considering decisions. The statements report the concern's results for a specified period in terms of assets and liabilities. Identify the statements supported by this role.
(A) The information can help the shareholder understand profitability and financial position.
(B) The primary objective is to guarantee that every decision made using the statements is correct.
(C) The decision-support role includes external parties as well as shareholders.
(D) Only shareholders are within the stated group of users.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
An undertaking is compiling information for its Statement of profit and loss for a specific period. Which pair of items should it report to show the operational results for that period?

An analyst has only a company's financial statements and wants to assess its industrial climate and quality of work. Consider the statements.
(A) The statements alone cannot directly establish whether the industrial climate is favourable.
(B) The statements alone cannot directly establish the quality of work.
(C) A monetary labour-cost figure itself reports the qualitative condition of industrial relations.
(D) Industrial-relations information is included in the statements as qualitative information.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company’s balance sheet shows three assets at ₹5,00,000, ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000. In a forced liquidation, they realise ₹4,20,000, ₹2,50,000 and ₹2,00,000, respectively. These are the only assets considered, and no other proceeds or costs apply. What is the total shortfall of liquidation proceeds from the amounts shown in the balance sheet?

Match List-I with List-II. Rule: loans repayable on demand or with original tenure not more than 12 months/operating cycle are short-term borrowings. The operating cycle is 12 months.
List-I
(A) Repayable on demand
(B) Original tenure 12 months; not on demand
(C) Original tenure 13 months; not on demand
(D) Original tenure 8 months; not on demand
List-II
(I) Short-term by 12-month tenure
(II) Short-term status not established by this rule
(III) Short-term by demand

ideas.body:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Assess current profitability and operational efficiency to judge the firm’s financial health.
(B) Ascertain the relative importance of components of the firm’s financial position.
(C) Identify reasons for a change in profitability or financial position.
(D) Judge the firm’s ability to repay debt and assess its short-term and long-term liquidity.

List-II
(I) Which components have greater or lesser importance in the firm’s financial position?
(II) What explains the change in the firm’s profitability or financial position?
(III) How able is the firm to repay debt, and what is its short-term and long-term liquidity position?
(IV) How profitable and operationally efficient is the firm, overall and across its departments, for judging its financial health?

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Consider the following statements about the purposes of financial statement analysis.
(A) It may assess the current profitability and operational efficiency of a firm as a whole and of its departments.
(B) It may ascertain the relative importance of different components of the firm’s financial position.
(C) It may identify reasons for changes in profitability or financial position.
(D) Its purpose is limited to judging the ability to repay long-term debt and excludes short-term liquidity.
Which of the above statements are correct?

A company's balance sheet lists the following asset figures for Year 1 and Year 2: tangible fixed assets ₹14 and ₹8; intangible assets ₹3 and ₹2; inventories ₹5 and ₹4; cash and cash equivalents ₹2 and ₹1. Total assets are ₹24 in Year 1 and ₹15 in Year 2. In a common-size balance sheet, what percentage of total assets is represented by intangible assets in Year 1?

Match each item in a common-size statement with its base or use.
List-I
(A) Balance-sheet asset
(B) Balance-sheet liability
(C) Profit-and-loss expenditure
(D) Common-size analysis for comparing differently sized enterprises
List-II
(I) Percentage of revenue from operations
(II) Percentage of total assets
(III) Percentage of total liabilities
(IV) Insight into financial-statement structure
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A company prepares figures for two periods using different accounting principles and plans to present them comparatively. What should it disclose?

A company reports revenue from operations of ₹8,00,000 and a specified expenditure of ₹2,00,000 in Year 1; in Year 2, the corresponding figures are ₹10,00,000 and ₹2,20,000. It prepares a separate common-size statement of profit and loss for each year. What percentage of revenue from operations does this expenditure represent in Year 1 and Year 2, respectively?

An analyst is preparing common-size statements to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two differently sized companies in the same industry. Arrange these steps in the correct order:
(A) Identify the common item for each financial statement.
(B) Express each item as a percentage of that common item.
(C) Compare the resulting percentages with corresponding percentages for the other company.
(D) Use the comparison to compare the companies’ operating and financing characteristics.
Choose the correct sequence.

A company prepares a common-size balance sheet. Its total assets are ₹40 lakh, including tangible fixed assets of ₹16 lakh; its revenue from operations is ₹64 lakh. What percentage of total assets is represented by tangible fixed assets?

A company reports revenue from operations of ₹12 lakh and expenditure on the same item of ₹6 lakh in Year 1. In Year 2, the corresponding figures are ₹15 lakh and ₹6.75 lakh. Using revenue from operations as the base in each year’s common-size statement of profit and loss, which interpretation is correct?

An analyst reviews a firm’s balance sheets and statements of profit and loss for 2024–25 and 2025–26. Both years use the same accounting principles. The analyst wants the reported figures for both periods presented comparatively to trace the direction of change, rather than expressing items as percentages of a common item. Which tool and analysis label fit this purpose?

A company prepares common-size balance sheets using total assets as the common item. Equipment is ₹40 lakh of total assets of ₹100 lakh in Year 1, and ₹60 lakh of total assets of ₹200 lakh in Year 2. By how many percentage points did equipment’s share of total assets change from Year 1 to Year 2?

An economist compares the financial statements of several firms to investigate whether economic power is concentrated and whether their financial policies have pitfalls. Which conclusion is this analysis specifically intended to support?

A company prepares a common-size balance sheet using total assets as the base. Total assets are ₹100 lakh in Year 1 and ₹150 lakh in Year 2; equipment is ₹40 lakh and ₹45 lakh, respectively. Equipment is reported as 40% and 30% of total assets, respectively. Which interpretation is correct?
The equipment amount fell, and its share fell by 10 percentage points.
The equipment amount rose, and its share rose by 10 percentage points.
The equipment amount rose, and its share fell by 10 percentage points.
The equipment amount stayed the same, and its share fell by 10 percentage points.

An economist is preparing a brief on the role of financial-statement analysis. Arrange the statements as a reasoning chain from the analysis to possible governmental use. Treat them as logical steps, not historical events.
(A) Such actions may include licensing and controls.
(B) First, financial statements of various firms are analysed.
(C) From this analysis, an economist can judge the concentration of economic power and pitfalls in financial policies.
(D) Besides enabling those judgements, the analysis provides a basis for governmental actions.
Choose the correct sequence.

ideas.body: A company reports the following figures: total assets are ₹24 lakh in Year 1 and ₹15 lakh in Year 2; inventories are ₹5 lakh in Year 1 and ₹4 lakh in Year 2. What percentage of total assets is represented by Year 1 inventories in a common-size balance sheet? Give your answer to two decimal places.

A company presents its balance-sheet figures for two periods side by side. It used the same accounting principles in both periods. Consider the following statements:
(A) The figures meet the stated condition for being comparative data.
(B) Expressing each item as a percentage of a common item is the defining basis of a comparative statement.
(C) If different accounting principles are used in two periods, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.
(D) The comparison of figures for different periods is called vertical analysis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Which statements correctly describe comparative statements?
(A) They show a firm’s profitability and financial position for different periods in comparative form.
(B) The financial data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used to prepare the statements.
(C) If accounting principles differ, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.
(D) Comparative analysis is also known as vertical analysis.

A firm presents its balance sheet and statement of profit and loss for two periods in comparative form. It uses the same accounting principles in both periods. Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) The comparative figures can indicate the trend and direction of the firm’s financial position and operating results.
(B) Financial data can be comparative even when different accounting principles are used and the difference is not disclosed in a footnote.
(C) The data meet the same-accounting-principles condition for being comparative.
(D) This analysis is also known as vertical analysis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Company P and Company Q have total assets of ₹10,00,000 and ₹5,00,000, respectively. Inventory is 20% of total assets in each company’s common-size balance sheet. Which interpretation is correct?

Consider the following statements about common-size statements:
(A) In a common-size balance sheet, liabilities are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) A common-size statement prepared for successive periods can show changes in the respective percentages over time.
(C) Common-size analysis can help compare enterprises that differ substantially in size by providing insight into the structure of their financial statements.
(D) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company presents financial statements for two periods in comparative form. It applied different accounting principles in the two periods and has not disclosed this difference. Consider the following statements:
(A) The financial data are comparative despite the difference in accounting principles.
(B) The deviation in accounting principles should be mentioned in a footnote.
(C) Financial data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used.
(D) A footnote makes the accounting principles used in the two periods the same.
Choose the correct answer:

An analyst is reviewing the following features of common-size statements. Which combination of statements is correct?
(A) Each item in a common-size statement is expressed as a percentage of a common item.
(B) Common-size analysis is also known as horizontal analysis.
(C) Common-size statements can be used to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry.
(D) Common-size statements are useful for inter-firm comparisons but not for comparing different years within one firm.

A company is preparing a common-size balance sheet and a common-size statement of profit and loss. Consider the following statements about the percentage bases to use:
(A) Inventory in the balance sheet is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) Each liability item in the balance sheet is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities.
(C) An expenditure item in the statement of profit and loss is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(D) An expenditure item in the statement of profit and loss is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Consider the following statements about the bases used in common-size statements:
(A) In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.
(C) In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.
(D) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A firm presents its balance sheets for two periods in comparative form. It applied one accounting principle differently in the two periods. What should it do about this difference?

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) A firm presents its balance sheet and statement of profit and loss in comparative form for two periods; the figures indicate trends and direction.
(B) An analyst compares the operating and financing characteristics of two differently sized companies in the same industry using common-base percentages.
(C) The accounting principles used in statements being compared differ, and the departure is disclosed in a footnote.
(D) The analysis that expresses each financial statement item as a percentage of a common item is given a particular name.

List-II
(I) Common size statements facilitate comparison of operating and financing characteristics of differently sized companies in the same industry.
(II) Comparative statements show financial position or profitability for different periods, and their figures indicate trends and direction.
(III) Comparative figures require the same accounting principles; departures are mentioned in a footnote.
(IV) Common size analysis is also known as vertical analysis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An analyst is preparing a common-size balance sheet for two years. Arrange these actions in the correct sequence:
(A) Work out each item’s percentage of its relevant total.
(B) List the absolute rupee figures for the two years.
(C) Choose the applicable common base of 100: total assets for asset items and total liabilities for liability items.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Two firms in the same industry differ in size, and statements are available for each of two years. Which method permits comparison of their operating and financing characteristics across firms and years on a common base?

A company prepares comparative statements for Years 1, 2 and 3. It uses the same accounting principles in Years 1 and 2, but changes one principle before Year 3; a Year 3 footnote discloses this change. Which conclusion follows for the two adjacent-year comparisons?

A firm reports revenue of ₹8,00,000 and operating expenses of ₹2,00,000 in Year 1. In Year 2, it reports revenue of ₹10,00,000 and operating expenses of ₹3,00,000. For a common-size comparison, use revenue as the common item in each year. What change in operating expenses as a percentage of revenue is shown from Year 1 to Year 2?

List-I
(A) Activity ratios

(I) Indicates the number of times inventory is converted into revenue from operations during an accounting period

For a 365-day accounting period, a firm’s trade payables comprise only creditors and bills payable. At the beginning of the period, creditors were ₹70,000 and bills payable were ₹30,000. At the end, creditors were ₹90,000 and bills payable were ₹50,000. Net purchases for the period were ₹6,00,000; no separate credit-purchase figure is provided. Use the arithmetic mean of beginning and ending trade payables. What was the firm’s average payment period, rounded to the nearest whole day?

A company’s inventory turnover ratio rose from 4 times to 8 times. During the period with the higher ratio, it bought inventory in small lots and sold goods quickly at low margins to realise cash. Both ratios are calculated on the same basis. Which conclusion is most defensible?

ideas.body:
In the indirect method, cash flow from operating activities starts with net profit/loss. Since the Statement of Profit and Loss is prepared on an accrual basis and includes non-operating and non-cash items, net profit/loss is adjusted to arrive at cash flows from operating activities. Arrange the following steps in their logical order:
(A) Adjust net profit/loss for the identified non-operating and non-cash items.
(B) Begin with net profit/loss.
(C) Identify the non-operating and non-cash items included in the Statement of Profit and Loss.
(D) Arrive at cash flows from operating activities.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

A flood caused a non-recurring loss at Nira Ltd.; for this question, the flood event is treated as an extraordinary item. The company’s only cash outflows directly arising from the flood were ₹2,40,000 for disposal of flood-damaged inventory and site clean-up, ₹1,35,000 for emergency repairs, and ₹75,000 for temporary storage. It also received ₹90,000 insurance compensation for the same event and paid ₹50,000 for routine maintenance unrelated to the flood. What total gross cash outflow arising from the extraordinary event should be calculated for separate disclosure? Do not offset receipts or include unrelated payments.

A garment manufacturer reports cash from operations of ₹18,00,000 for the year. During the same period, it needs ₹4,00,000 to maintain its operating capability, ₹3,00,000 for dividends, ₹5,00,000 for new investments and ₹4,00,000 for loan repayments. Assume all amounts are cash amounts for the same period; these are the only requirements being assessed; and current-period cash from operations is the only source available for meeting them, with no opening cash or external financing used. Which conclusion follows?

Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) A non-financial company receives cash on disposal of machinery used as a fixed asset.
(B) A financial enterprise makes cash advances and loans to third parties as part of its operating activities.
(C) A company pays cash to acquire machinery for use as a fixed asset.
(D) A non-financial company makes a cash loan to a third party.
List-II
(I) Investing cash inflow from disposal of a fixed asset
(II) Operating cash flow from advances and loans made by a financial enterprise
(III) Investing cash outflow to acquire a fixed asset
(IV) Investing cash outflow for a loan or advance to a third party by a non-financial enterprise

List-I
(A) Method characterised by disclosure of major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments

(D) Statement about the availability under the indirect method of information useful in estimating future cash flows

(I) Direct method
(II) Adjustment of net profit or loss for non-cash transactions, deferrals or accruals of operating cash receipts, and income or expenses associated with investing or financing cash flows
(III) Net profit or loss before taxation and extraordinary items

A company’s Statement of Profit and Loss includes a depreciation expense. For calculating cash flows from operating activities by the indirect method, consider the following statements:
(A) Depreciation is a non-cash item.
(B) Depreciation is treated as a cash outflow from operating activities.
(C) Depreciation is added back to net profit when calculating cash flows from operating activities.
(D) Depreciation is added back because it is a cash outflow from financing activities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

(B) (A) and (C) only
(C) (B) and (D) only

A company incurs a non-recurring cash outflow associated with a flood loss. The activity from which the outflow arises is not specified.
Which statements correctly describe the outflow and its treatment?
(A) The cash flow should be classified and disclosed separately as arising from the relevant operating, investing or financing activity.
(B) Separate disclosure helps users understand the nature of the item and its effect on present and future cash flows.
(C) The outflow must be classified as an investing activity because it is associated with a flood loss.
(D) A flood loss is an example of an extraordinary item.

A non-financial enterprise prepares a cash flow statement. Each transaction below is a cash transaction. The dividend is received from an investment in another enterprise. The shares mentioned in (C) and the debt instruments mentioned in (D) relate to another enterprise; the shares are held for trading purposes, and the debt instruments are not held for trading purposes. None of the investments or instruments mentioned is included in cash equivalents. Select the correct statements.
(A) Cash interest received on loans and advances made to third parties is an investing cash outflow.
(B) A cash dividend received from an investment in another enterprise is an investing cash inflow.
(C) A cash payment to acquire shares held for trading purposes is classified as an investing cash outflow.
(D) A cash payment to acquire debt instruments not held for trading purposes is classified as an investing cash outflow.

An enterprise is preparing a cash flow statement for an accounting period. Consider the following statements about its presentation.
(A) The statement reports the change in the position of cash and cash equivalents over the accounting period.
(B) Activities contributing to this change are classified as operating, investing and financing activities.
(C) Under each activity heading, it is sufficient to show only the net cash flow (or use), rather than full details of inflows and outflows.
(D) The aggregate net cash flow (or use) is worked out from the net amounts of the operating, investing and financing activities.

ideas.body: A firm’s employees joined for different reasons: some value competitive salaries, others peer recognition, and others personal growth. The employees are expected to contribute to one common organisational goal. The manager accommodates their differing personal goals and arranges their work so that each person’s effort supports that common goal. Which conclusion best describes coordination in this situation?
Employees in an organisation may have personal goals, while the organisation has its own objectives. Which management action is identified as promoting harmony between them?

Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Social objective of an organisation
(B) Financial need of personnel
(C) Social need of personnel
(D) Higher-level need of personnel
List-II
(I) Peer recognition
(II) Personal growth and development
(III) Creation of benefit for society, including employment opportunities for underprivileged sections
(IV) Competitive salaries and perks
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each coordination characteristic in List-I with the situation in List-II that best illustrates it.

List-I
(A) Coordination integrates group efforts
(B) Coordination ensures unity of action
(C) Coordination is a continuous process
(D) Coordination is an all-pervasive function

List-II
(I) Coordination is arranged at each management level because the activities of different departments are interdependent.
(II) Coordination starts during planning and continues through controlling, rather than being treated as a single event.
(III) Groups with diverse work interests are brought together into purposeful activity, with a common focus so that performance follows the plan and schedule.
(IV) Coordination binds departments so that all their actions are directed towards the organisation's common purpose.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A unit’s review records show that its targets were met according to plans. Employees report being happy and satisfied, and work proceeds in an orderly way rather than in chaos. An observer can see these outcomes but cannot see management as an object. Which interpretation best explains the case?

While production is under way, a department manager drafts a plan for the next output period, reallocates materials for current work, assigns an available worker, instructs the team and checks current output. In this case, these activities are identified, respectively, as planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling. The same manager carries them out during an overlapping period. Which conclusion follows?

At a company, the senior-most executives include managers heading finance and marketing. Consider the following statements about its top management:
(A) Top management coordinates departmental activities according to each department’s own objectives rather than the organisation’s overall objectives.
(B) Top management analyses the business environment and its implications for the firm’s survival.
(C) Top management implements and controls plans and strategies formulated by middle management.
(D) Top management formulates overall organisational goals and strategies for their achievement.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A business is preparing a management note. Arrange the following statements from the overall purpose of resource use, to the basic objective, to the objective beyond mere survival, and finally to the long-run objective.
(A) Management seeks profit, which is essential for covering costs and business risks.
(B) Management aims to use human and material resources to maximum possible advantage to fulfil the business’s economic objectives.
(C) Management seeks enough revenue to cover costs so that the organisation survives.
(D) Management exploits the organisation’s growth potential for long-run prospects.
Choose the correct sequence from the options below:

A project team includes members who joined the organisation for different personal reasons. One member argues that effective teamwork is possible only if everyone had the same reason for joining. Which response best reflects management as a group activity?

Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Management ensures that an organisation earns enough revenue to cover its costs.
(B) Management ensures that the organisation makes a profit.
(C) Management exploits the organisation’s growth potential to remain in the industry.
(D) The organisation’s main objective is to use human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage.
List-II
(I) Main objective of the organisation
(II) Survival
(III) Profit
(IV) Growth
Each entry in List-II is to be used once.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Arrange the following actions in the order in which they move from top management towards the workforce:
(i) Supervisors pass instructions from middle management to workers.
(ii) Top management formulates overall organisational goals and strategies.
(iii) Middle management interprets top management’s policies and carries out its plans.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company’s senior-most executive team is reviewing its responsibility after a business decision affects activities across departments and has an impact on society. Consider the following statements about the team:
(A) Its responsibility is limited to decisions made personally by the chairperson.
(B) It is responsible for all activities of the business.
(C) It is responsible for the business’s impact on society.
(D) Its responsibility ends whenever an activity is carried out within an individual department.
Which statements correctly describe the team’s responsibilities?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A business earns revenue equal to its costs and reports no profit. Which statements are correct?
(A) The main objective of an organisation is to utilise human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage to fulfil its economic objectives.
(B) Because revenue equals costs, the business has achieved the profit objective.
(C) Its revenue meets the condition for survival.
(D) Remaining in the industry does not require management to fully exploit the organisation’s growth potential.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A review panel considers three bodies: (i) a commercial venture, stipulated to be an economic organisation; (ii) a neighbourhood arts association, stipulated to be a social organisation; and (iii) a political party, stipulated to be a political organisation. Which statements are consistent with the principle that management is all pervasive?
(A) Management is relevant to the commercial venture.
(B) Management is relevant to the arts association even though it is social.
(C) The political party is outside the scope of management unless it also has an economic purpose.
(D) Of these three bodies, only the commercial venture requires management.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An organisation’s senior executives frame its policies. A division head is subordinate to these executives and superior to first-line managers. Which responsibility belongs to the division head in relation to those policies?

Match each management review finding in List-I with its most direct implication in List-II.
List-I
(A) Revenue just covers costs; no profit is reported.
(B) Management seeks profit to cover costs and business risks.
(C) Management seeks long-run continuation in the industry.
(D) Management reviews whether human and material resources are used to maximum advantage.
List-II
(I) Exploiting the organisation’s growth potential
(II) Fulfilling the business’s economic objectives through resource use
(III) Meeting the basic survival requirement
(IV) Profit’s role in covering costs and risks and supporting continued successful operation
Each entry in List-II is to be used once.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A regional learning centre finds that changes in local social and economic conditions have altered the educational needs of the community it serves. Which response best reflects management as a dynamic function?
After a unit’s annual plan has been prepared, the unit continues its work throughout the year. Which conclusion about management follows?

A retail venture states increasing sales as its goal, while a community organisation states providing adult literacy as its goal. In each organisation, staff members propose activities they individually prefer. Which management approach best follows from these stated goals?

ideas.body:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Meaning of principles of management
(B) Nature of management principles
(C) Why understanding their significance matters
(D) Significance of management principles
List-II
(I) Proper understanding of their significance is essential to make sound decisions by managers.
(II) General guidelines that can be used for conduct in work places under certain situations.
(III) Formed by practice; general guidelines; universal; flexible; behavioural; contingent; and cause and effect relationship.
(IV) Increase in efficiency; optimum utilisation of resources; scientific decision making; adaptation to changing environment; fulfilling social responsibilities; research and development; training managers; and effective administration.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Which of the following is a technique of scientific management associated with Taylor?

At a manufacturing firm, the production team has a daily output target. One employee asks to leave two hours early each day while retaining the same pay; granting the request would make the team miss that target. The manager’s authority to set the schedule is not disputed, and the manager rejects the personal exception. Which Fayol principle is most directly illustrated?

Match each management situation in List-I with the principle in List-II that it best illustrates.

List-I
(A) A company allows branch managers to decide routine local matters, while the head office retains final authority.
(B) A manager refuses to misuse her powers for a family benefit at the cost of the company's general interest, thereby setting an example for workers.
(C) An employee communicates with a colleague in another department by following the formal authority route through the intervening levels.
(D) A company fixes employees' wages at a level that provides a reasonable standard of living and remains within the company's paying capacity.

List-II
(I) Scalar Chain
(II) Centralisation and Decentralisation
(III) Remuneration of Employees
(IV) Subordination of Individual Interest to General Interest

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each organisational arrangement in List-I with the corresponding Fayol principle in a contemporary (NOW) classification.
List-I
(A) Employees, rather than managers, are empowered.
(B) Subordinates report to multiple bosses.
(C) Functions have multiple plans and multiple bosses.
(D) Rewards are performance-based.
List-II
(I) Unity of Direction
(II) Remuneration of personnel
(III) Authority and Responsibility
(IV) Unity of Command
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A packing unit wants to reduce both packing time and wrapping-material waste. The manager can trial two proposed arrangements of the packing steps. The arrangements can be tested on comparable batches using the same workers, tools and input quantities; elapsed time and wrapping material used can be recorded. Which action best applies a scientific approach to deciding between the arrangements?

A company reviews its remuneration policy. Management first checks that the pay will provide employees with at least a reasonable standard of living and remain within the company’s paying capacity. Arrange the following stages in the order supported by the principle.
(A) The company’s working becomes smooth.
(B) Management checks that the pay meets the two stated requirements.
(C) A congenial atmosphere and good relations between workers and management result.
(D) The remuneration is just and equitable.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
Which statement correctly describes the general nature and role of principles of management?

A manager seeks to replace traditional work methods with one standard method. The manager considers these actions:
I. Follow the standard method throughout the organisation
II. Investigate traditional methods through work-study
III. Develop a standard method
IV. Unify the best practices

Which sequence arranges the actions from first to last?

A company is organising activities that serve a shared organisational objective. Arrange the following stages of applying unity of direction, beginning with establishing the shared objective and ending with coordinated execution.

(I) Assign one head and one plan to each group of activities having the same objective.
(II) Coordinate and focus the efforts of all units towards the common objective.
(III) Identify the objective shared by the activities.
(IV) Group together activities that have the same objective.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A manager faces a workplace situation and consults management principles before choosing a course of action and putting it into effect. Which statement best describes the role of those principles in this situation?
Which of the following is named as a principle of Taylor’s scientific management?

Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Science, not the rule of thumb
(B) Harmony, not discord
(C) Cooperation, not individualism
(D) Development of each person to greatest efficiency and prosperity
List-II
(I) A manager rejects a method chosen solely because it is customary and selects one supported by scientific study.
(II) Managers and workers seek harmonious relations rather than discord.
(III) Workers and managers coordinate their efforts instead of acting individually.
(IV) A manager develops each employee towards the greatest efficiency and prosperity.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm’s operating environment changes. Its managers review a decision made under the earlier conditions and, using management principles as guidance, revise the decision so that it suits the changed conditions. The case states no separate efficiency target, resource-utilisation outcome or research activity. Which significance of management principles is most directly illustrated?

A customer-support company originally assigns each worker one narrow stage of handling a service request. In a redesign, each worker’s job covers a broader range of stages instead of one specialised stage. Decision-making authority and the reward system remain unchanged. Which change in the division-of-work comparison does this redesign illustrate?

A distribution firm is reviewing recurring delivery delays. Its manager has stated the delay as the problem and prepared two possible route plans. Before selecting or implementing either plan, the manager estimates the likely effect of each on delivery time and fuel use. Which step in the scientific approach is being applied at this point?

A firm is deciding whether to treat management principles as fixed instructions across different workplace situations. Consider the following statements:
(A) Management principles are formed by practice.
(B) Their nature includes flexibility and contingency.
(C) Their universal nature requires identical, unchanging application in every situation.
(D) Their nature includes a cause-and-effect relationship.
Which statements correctly describe the nature of management principles?

A manager has authority to secure a personal benefit for a family member, but doing so would be at the cost of the larger general interest of the workers and company. She refrains from doing so and acts as an example to the workers. Consider the following statements:
(A) Her conduct is exemplary behaviour of the kind described.
(B) Her conduct will raise her stature in the eyes of the workers.
(C) Her conduct will ensure the workers show the same behaviour.
(D) Her conduct gives priority to her family’s interest over the larger general interest.
Which statements are supported?
A factory wants to replace its supervisors’ separate rules of thumb for a recurring task with one organisation-wide method. Which procedure is consistent with scientific management?

ideas.body: A firm is reviewing the procedures for one of its business activities. It learns that a government rule applicable to that activity has been amended. Customer tastes, technology and political conditions have not changed. Which consideration is directly relevant to the firm’s response?

A firm is designing a compliance-monitoring register. It includes legislation passed by the government, administrative orders issued by government authorities, court judgments, and decisions of commissions and agencies at central, state and local levels. Which interpretation of the register’s coverage is correct?

Match List-I with List-II on the stated business-environment changes and their implications.

List-I
(A) Increase in life expectancy and awareness for health care
(B) New health products and services
(C) Technological improvements
(D) Changes in fashions and tastes of consumers

List-II
(I) May render existing products obsolete
(II) May shift demand from existing products to new ones
(III) May increase demand for health products and services
(IV) Have, in turn, changed people’s lifestyles

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A firm reviewing the external factors relevant to a proposed project notes that elected government representatives hold a favourable attitude towards business. Which conclusion is best supported?

A company categorises four external developments as follows:
(i) A government authority issues an administrative order applicable to the company.
(ii) A court delivers a judgment concerning the company’s operations.
(iii) The government announces a change in the extent of its intervention in business.
(iv) Consumer preferences for the company’s product shift.
Which pair should be classified as legal-environment elements?
A government regulation requires a business to include a specified warning in its product advertisements. Which dimension of the business environment does this requirement illustrate?

A business enterprise is reviewing a state-level court judgment that sets a procedure it is required to follow. The judgment is the only external development in this case; no political change, social shift or technological development is described. Which dimension of the business environment does the judgment represent?
A business is classifying external developments by environment dimension. Which development belongs to the legal environment?

A business group compares two successive periods in the same country. In the first period, there is political unrest and threats to law and order; in the second, there is political stability and peace. Assume that no other relevant conditions change, including legal conditions and court judgments. The group wants to map this political change to business predictability, business people’s confidence and their willingness to invest. Which sequence is supported?

An advertiser is subject to a mandatory regulation requiring specified information in an advertisement. It publishes the advertisement without that information. Consider the following statements:
(A) The advertiser must include the specified information to comply with the applicable requirement.
(B) Failure to include it can expose the business enterprise to legal problems.
(C) The advertiser may treat the mandatory requirement as optional.
(D) Non-compliance with a law is not a possible source of legal problems.
Choose the correct answer:
(A) Statements (A) and (B) only
(B) Statements (A) and (C) only
(C) Statements (B) and (D) only
(D) Statements (C) and (D) only

Match List-I with List-II by pairing each business-environment change with the effect associated with it.
List-I
(A) Increase in taxes by government
(B) Technological improvements
(C) Political uncertainty
(D) Changes in fashions and tastes of consumers
List-II
(I) May create fear in the minds of investors
(II) May render existing products obsolete
(III) May make things expensive to buy
(IV) May shift demand from existing products to new ones
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) An advertisement of alcoholic beverages
(B) A cigarette packet
(C) An advertisement of baby food
(D) A business enterprise’s non-compliance with a law
List-II
(I) Must inform the potential buyer that mother’s milk is the best
(II) Is prohibited
(III) Carries the statutory warning ‘Cigarette smoking is injurious to health’
(IV) Can land the business enterprise in legal problems
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A business prepares a cigarette advertisement. Assume that the applicable regulation requires the statutory warning and that omitting it constitutes non-compliance. Arrange the following stages in logical order, from the applicable requirement to its possible consequence.
(A) The regulation requires the statutory warning in the advertisement.
(B) The advertiser omits the required warning.
(C) The advertisement is non-compliant with the regulation.
(D) The business may face legal problems due to non-compliance.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Assume a country has political stability and peace. Arrange the following stages in the resulting progression, from the first consequence to the final outcome:
(A) People gain confidence to invest.
(B) Investment is made in long-term projects.
(C) New businesses are created through those projects.
(D) The economy grows.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II on the basis of the business environment dimension or element each development represents. Each description states the complete development; do not infer any unstated formal direction or legal instrument.

List-I
(A) Government officials express a favourable attitude towards business, without issuing a formal direction.
(B) The government passes legislation governing a business matter.
(C) A government authority issues an administrative order governing a business matter.
(D) A commission at the state level renders a decision concerning a business matter.

List-II
(I) Political environment—attitudes of government officials
(II) Legal environment—legislation passed by the government
(III) Legal environment—administrative orders issued by government authorities
(IV) Legal environment—decisions rendered by commissions

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A business is filing decisions rendered by commissions and agencies under three government-level labels. Arrange the labels from the broadest level to the most local level.
(A) Local
(B) Centre
(C) State
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
