ideas.body:
Consider the following statements about procedures, methods and rules in an organisation:
(A) A procedure specifies the steps to be followed in particular circumstances.
(B) A method specifies the manner in which a task has to be performed.
(C) A rule specifies the manner in which a task has to be performed.
(D) A rule states exactly what has to be done.

Select the correct statements.

An organisation is formulating a strategy. Consider the following statements:
(A) The business environment needs to be considered while formulating the strategy.
(B) Changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment affect the organisation’s strategy.
(C) Considering the business environment replaces the need to determine long-term objectives and allocate resources.
(D) The business environment needs to be considered only if the organisation plans to enter a new line of business.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A comprehensive plan is being prepared to accomplish an organisation’s objectives. Which set correctly identifies its three dimensions?

A business is formulating a comprehensive plan. It has determined its long-term objective, adopted a course of action and considered the business environment. However, it has not decided what resources are necessary to achieve the objective. Which dimension of the comprehensive plan remains incomplete?

A firm is planning production of one product. Four managers are involved in preparing one common plan, and each has proposed a different forecast of the product’s future demand. No forecast is stated to be more accurate than the others. What should the managers do to use these forecasts as planning premises?

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) The role of objectives in planning
(B) The future position management seeks to reach
(C) The required quantitative expression of objectives
(D) The period attached to a statement of desired results

List-II
(I) Objectives represent the end point of planning.
(II) Objectives describe a desired future position.
(III) Objectives should be measurable in quantitative terms.
(IV) Desired results are to be achieved within a given time period.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each managerial situation in List-I with the planning idea in List-II.

List-I
(A) A manager sets a target and then develops actions directed towards it.
(B) A manager chooses one course from several available courses of action.
(C) Before starting work, a manager decides what to do and how to do it.
(D) Managers at all levels prepare plans for their respective work.

List-II
(I) Planning is undertaken by managers at all levels.
(II) Planning involves choosing from alternative courses of action.
(III) Planning involves setting objectives and developing courses of action to achieve them.
(IV) Planning means deciding in advance what to do and how to do it.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company is preparing a long-term plan for launching a new service. The planning team identifies these actions:
(A) Set the long-term outcome the organisation intends to achieve.
(B) Set aside the staff, funds and equipment needed to achieve that outcome.
(C) Select the course of action for pursuing that outcome.
Arrange the actions in the order in which the dimensions of a comprehensive plan are presented.

Arrange the following plan types in the order in which they appear in the classification based on what plans seek to achieve:
(A) Programme
(B) Strategy
(C) Budget
(D) Procedure

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A case includes a government-owned organisation, a privately owned business, a small business and a company with big plans. Consider the following statements about planning:
(A) Planning is required in both government-owned and privately owned organisations.
(B) Planning is relevant to both a small business and a company with big plans.
(C) Planning is required only in privately owned organisations.
(D) A small business needs plans only if it operates nationwide.
Select the correct statements.

An educational institution has already stated its broad admission policy. To handle applications that lack a required document, its staff need an ordered sequence of steps to follow in that particular circumstance. Which type of plan should the institution prepare?

A company states a broad aim to become one of the leading companies in its field. It has not yet specified any actions for carrying out this aim and intends to pursue it. What is the appropriate next planning step?

Assume each situation results from planning. Match each situation with the way planning reduces overlapping and wasteful activities.

List-I
(A) Production and logistics align their schedules for one project.
(B) Staff receive clear instructions about task responsibilities.
(C) A duplicate report is removed.
(D) Planned hand-offs occur without breaks.

List-II
(I) Coordination across departments
(II) Clarity that avoids confusion
(III) Fewer redundant activities
(IV) Smooth work without interruption

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the planning idea in List-II.

List-I
(A) Managers assume future demand before drafting a plan.
(B) A plan is drafted using assumptions as its starting material.
(C) Forecasting is used to gather information on future demand.
(D) All planning managers use the same agreed assumptions.

List-II
(I) Forecasting gathers information for premises.
(II) Assumptions are the base material for plans.
(III) Managers use common assumptions.
(IV) Future assumptions are called premises.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An organisation is cascading objectives into unit planning. Arrange the stages in the logical order from setting organisation-wide objectives to directing activities.
(A) Each unit formulates its own objectives with the overall goals in view.
(B) Other managerial activities are directed towards achieving the objectives.
(C) Top management sets broad objectives for the organisation.
(D) These objectives guide overall business planning.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Match each situation (List-I) to the policy idea (List-II).
List-I
(A) Purchase policy eases a supplier-selection problem.
(B) Pricing policy sets limits; a manager chooses a price.
(C) Recruitment policy guides decisions implementing strategy.
(D) Policy states the response to a particular problem.
List-II
(I) Implementation guidance
(II) Easier issue resolution
(III) Parameters allowing managerial discretion
(IV) General response to a problem
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A service organisation has set a launch target. Its design and outreach teams are selecting activities that pull in different directions. Management issues a shared plan that aligns both teams’ work with the target. The case involves no anticipated change, duplicated task or comparison with a performance standard. Which immediate contribution of planning is demonstrated?
Before a task begins, a supervisor devises a new method for carrying it out and decides how the work will proceed. Which idea about planning is most directly illustrated?

A furniture workshop supervisor gives workers directions for sanding tabletops. The task and required result are already set; the directions specify how the sanding is to be carried out, not steps for a particular circumstance or an exact requirement such as a fixed reporting time. What type of plan do these directions represent?
A firm sets the objective of increasing sales. Managers in its sales and production teams use it to guide decisions about their work. Which function of the objective is illustrated?
An organisation has a desired goal for a new customer-support process but makes no plan for the work. Its employees independently choose incompatible priorities. Which outcome follows most directly?

A company is deciding whether to continue in its existing line of business or add a new line. Before finalising its strategy, managers review changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment. Which planning principle does this review apply?

ideas.body: A company prepares a chart that names each employee's immediate superior and reporting channel. After the chart is shared, employees know whom to approach with work-related questions. No tasks are redistributed, and no change in resource use or organisational size is described. Which importance of organising is most directly illustrated?

Consider the following statements about delegation:
(A) Delegation transfers authority from a superior to a subordinate.
(B) Delegation transfers authority from a subordinate to a superior.
(C) Delegation establishes superior-subordinate relationships that form the basis of management hierarchy.
(D) The extent of delegated authority helps determine the power enjoyed by each job position.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Arrange the following statements in the causal order in which a functional structure promotes efficiency in the utilisation of manpower, starting with its design feature.
(A) Employees perform similar tasks within a department and are able to improve performance.
(B) Efficiency in the utilisation of manpower is promoted.
(C) Similar or related jobs are grouped together.
(D) Emphasis on specific functions leads to occupational specialisation.
Choose the correct sequence:

In a workplace, employees form social ties through interaction and use those ties to communicate about a proposal. Assume the communication uses an informal network rather than a planned route. Arrange the following events in a logically supported sequence, from the origin of the network to its communication outcome.
(A) Employees interact socially.
(B) A network of social relationships arises from their interaction.
(C) Communication takes place through a route that is not planned.
(D) Information spreads faster and feedback is quick.

A firm groups its production, finance and marketing employees by function. Employees doing similar tasks coordinate smoothly within each department. However, each functional head prioritises that department’s interests over a stated enterprise-wide objective, and interaction between production and marketing has weakened.
Consider the following statements:
(A) Smooth coordination within departments does not rule out coordination problems between functionally differentiated departments.
(B) Similarity of tasks within a department guarantees that each functional head prioritises enterprise-wide objectives.
(C) Pursuing departmental interests at the expense of organisational interests can hinder interaction between departments.
(D) Smooth coordination within functions necessarily eliminates coordination problems across functions.
Which statements correctly interpret the situation?

A firm is organising a new unit. The teams' tasks are:
Team P: establish reporting relationships
Team Q: assign duties to employees
Team R: identify and divide the work
Team S: group activities into departments
The team labels do not indicate chronological order. Consider the following statements:
(A) Team R's task is the first step in the organising process.
(B) Team Q's task immediately precedes Team P's task.
(C) Team S's task follows Team Q's task.
(D) Team P's task is the final step.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company is organising its work through four separate decisions. Match each decision in List-I with the corresponding step in the organising process in List-II.
List-I
(A) Before deciding departments or job-holders, management breaks the total workload into identifiable activities.
(B) Activities with related features are grouped into departments, without yet naming the employees who will perform them.
(C) After the departments have been settled, specified duties are allotted to particular employees.
(D) For each position, the direct superior to whom its holder reports is recorded.
List-II
(I) Identification and division of work
(II) Departmentalisation
(III) Assignment of Duties
(IV) Establishing reporting relationships
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each description in List-I with the delegation element or condition in List-II.
List-I
(A) A right derived from formal position to direct a subordinate within the scope of the job
(B) An obligation to perform an assigned duty, arising from delegated authority
(C) Answerability for the outcome of an assigned task, arising from responsibility
(D) The authority granted for a job is aligned with the responsibility assigned for it
List-II
(I) Accountability
(II) Authority
(III) Commensurateness of authority with responsibility
(IV) Responsibility
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm groups related jobs into departments according to function. Match each situation in List-I with the corresponding advantage in List-II.
List-I
(A) A new employee’s training is limited to a narrow range of skills used in the assigned function.
(B) A redesign reduces the repeated performance of the same activity by different teams.
(C) The organisational structure gives a place to each of the firm’s different functions.
(D) Employees in one department perform similar tasks.
List-II
(I) Training becomes easier because the focus is on a limited range of skills.
(II) Minimal duplication of effort supports economies of scale and lower cost.
(III) Different functions receive due attention.
(IV) Similar tasks promote control and coordination within a department.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A supervisor delegates to an employee the authority to direct staff on routine scheduling, which is within the employee’s position. An organisational rule reserves purchase approvals to another role, but the supervisor also asks the employee to approve a purchase. Which action is within the employee’s authority?

Match each description in List-I with the corresponding organisational form or structure in List-II.
List-I
(A) An arrangement designed by management to achieve stated organisational goals.
(B) Relationships among employees that arise through their interaction at work.
(C) Activities grouped on the basis of functions.
(D) Activities grouped on the basis of products.
List-II
(I) Divisional structure
(II) Informal organisation
(III) Formal organisation
(IV) Functional structure
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Department head H delegates to team lead T authority to manage a project, including authority to assign a specified component to analyst A. T assigns responsibility for that component to A and grants A the authority needed to perform it. T then tells H that all accountability for the component has passed to A and that T is no longer accountable for its outcome. Which assessment of T’s claim is correct?

A department manager has authority in the formal organisation by virtue of her position. Separately, employees have formed a social network through their interactions, and they seek her advice in that network because of her personal qualities. Which basis explains her authority within the social network?

For a new unit, a manager is reviewing proposed bundles of actions. Assume each bundle lists all the actions it includes. Which bundle most completely represents organising as defined by its core components?

A manager has identified and divided the work and grouped the activities into departments. No other organising step has been completed, and no authority relationships have been established.
Consider the following statements:
(A) The work has been defined and grouped.
(B) Organising is complete once activities have been grouped.
(C) Establishing authority relationships is part of organising.
(D) All four listed steps of the organising process have been completed.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A manager formally assigns a task to a subordinate and delegates the authority needed to perform it. The manager then states that accountability for the task’s outcome has been transferred completely to the subordinate, leaving the manager with none. Which evaluation is supported?
In a workplace, management appoints R as a department manager. Separately, coworkers choose S, who holds no managerial post, to lead their informal group. Which conclusion is supported?

A company rule states that no employee, including a manager, may authorise a payment above ₹50,000. A manager assigns a subordinate responsibility for authorising a payment of ₹80,000 and instructs the subordinate to approve it. No exception to the rule is stated. Which conclusion best applies?

A new service unit has no established social ties among its employees. Before it opens, senior management creates a work arrangement specifically to help the unit function smoothly. Which feature of formal organisation is most directly illustrated?

A firm groups related jobs in a functional department. Assume its employees’ work requires a limited range of skills and that training focuses only on those skills. Which conclusion follows about employee training?

Arrange the statements in the causal sequence from the grouping of jobs to the resulting use of manpower.
(A) A functional structure groups similar or related jobs together.
(B) That grouping places emphasis on specific functions.
(C) This emphasis leads to occupational specialisation.
(D) Following this occupational specialisation, employees perform similar tasks within a department, promoting efficient manpower utilisation and enabling performance to improve.
Choose the correct sequence.

Assume a firm uses a functional structure and the employees considered work in one department. Consider the following statements:
(A) Similarity of tasks promotes control and coordination within that department.
(B) Similarity in the tasks being performed is the stated reason for this benefit.
(C) This control-and-coordination benefit is stated at the departmental level.
(D) This benefit is attributed to employees performing dissimilar tasks.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm uses a functional structure, grouping similar or related jobs. It attributes a reduction in costs to a decrease in duplicated effort. Which stated causal chain best explains the cost reduction?

A firm groups employees into separate purchasing, production and sales departments by function. When a customer changes an order, staff must exchange the revised details across these departments. Repeated hand-offs delay coordinated action. Which explanation best fits this problem as a possible disadvantage of the structure?

A firm uses a functional structure. Its production head gives the production department’s target priority over a stated company-wide objective, and the two targets conflict. Which limitation of the structure is most directly illustrated?

topics.text: Meaning and importance.
Steps in the process of organising.
Structure of organization – functional and divisional.

ideas.body:
Arrange the following stages in the order in which staffing responsibility is described as an organisation moves from a small organisation to a larger one:
(A) Managers in a small organisation may handle employees’ salaries, welfare and working conditions.
(B) The organisation grows and the number of persons employed increases.
(C) A separate human resource department is formed.
(D) Specialists in that department manage people.
Choose the correct sequence:

A new enterprise has completed planning and organising and has created its organisation structure. Arrange the following staffing activities in the order described:
(A) Recruitment
(B) Identification of the workforce requirement
(C) Placement
(D) Selection
Choose the correct sequence:

A firm’s two units use the same technology and face comparable operating conditions, but the quality of their human resources differs. When assessing their capacity to achieve organisational goals, which principle should guide the assessment?

An organisation is preparing employees to operate sophisticated equipment. It wants the training to imitate job realities while allowing learning without the risk or high costs that mistakes in real-life operation could cause. Which approach most directly meets both requirements?

A business has vacancies and is considering candidates from its existing workforce as well as candidates from outside. It seeks fresh talent and a wider choice of candidates. Consider the following statements:
(A) External sources of recruitment are used to obtain fresh talent and a wider choice.
(B) Recruitment from within the enterprise is internal recruitment.
(C) Transfers and promotions are important sources of internal recruitment.
(D) Recruitment from within the enterprise is external recruitment.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each staffing idea in List-I with the statement in List-II that expresses it.
List-I
(A) Human relations approach
(B) Prime concern of the staffing function
(C) Staffing in relation to positions in the organisation structure
(D) Staffing as a job-person matching function
List-II
(I) Timely fulfilment of manpower requirements
(II) Recognition of the human factor as the most important instrument of success in an organisation
(III) Filling the positions provided for in the organisation structure
(IV) Finding the right people for the right job
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An organisation has two vacancies. Its HR team identifies people who may be suitable and circulates vacancy notices inviting them to apply. After applications are received, the team compares candidates for the jobs. Which activity in the case represents recruitment?
A. Identifying prospective employees and stimulating them to apply
B. Assessing applicants and making the final match
C. Acquainting employees with work and developing their skills
D. Shifting an employee between jobs without a substantive change in responsibilities and status

A company arranges a classroom away from its actual work floor to recreate a department’s work environment. New employees practise with the same equipment, materials and files they will use in their jobs. Which training method best describes this arrangement?

A business is filling a vacancy through external recruitment. It has notified the vacancy, but no applications have arrived and selection has not begun. Which statement correctly describes when selection should be initiated?

Match each recruitment source in List-I with its described feature in List-II.
List-I
(A) Campus recruitment
(B) Recommendations of employees
(C) Labour contractors
(D) Web publishing
List-II
(I) Websites provide information about job seekers and job openings and are visited by prospective employees and organisations.
(II) Contractors can supply the required number of unskilled workers at short notice.
(III) Recruitment from educational institutions for various jobs.
(IV) Applicants introduced by present employees, or their friends and relatives, whose background is sufficiently known.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company is estimating staffing needs for two units. For Unit X, planned task volume and the number of employees available have both increased. For Unit Y, planned task volume is unchanged while the number of employees available has decreased. The directions of change are known, but their magnitudes are not. Which approach should the managers use to determine whether each unit’s manpower requirement is met?

A company compares two selection routes. Route A selected 15 employees; 13 met its selection-stage benchmark and 9 met the stated on-the-job performance standard after six months. Route B selected 10 employees; 8 met its selection-stage benchmark and 7 met the same on-the-job standard after six months. The employees worked in comparable roles and conditions. For this comparison, effectiveness is measured by the proportion of selected employees who meet the on-the-job standard. Which route has the higher effectiveness on this measure?

Match each activity or description with the staffing concept it primarily represents. Each concept is used once.

List-I
(A) Human resource personnel search for qualified people to work for the organisation.
(B) Managers throughout the organisation directly deal with and select people to work for it.
(C) Employees are helped to develop for efficient performance and career growth.
(D) The management function focuses on the human component of an organisation.

List-II
(I) Training and development
(II) Recruitment
(III) Staffing as a generic function of management
(IV) Staffing's focus on the human element

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II. Each case reports a specific result. Match it with the training-and-development purpose or outcome it directly illustrates.

List-I
(A) After a training intervention, the number of units produced per shift rises, while product quality is unchanged.
(B) After a training intervention, product quality improves, while the number of units produced per shift is unchanged.
(C) A development programme increases employees’ ability to perform duties they will take up in a later period; no current productivity or profit change is reported.
(D) Employee productivity improves, and higher profits follow; the case does not report a separate change in quantity or quality.

List-II
(I) Increasing an employee’s ability to perform to improve future performance.
(II) Enhancing employee productivity in terms of quantity.
(III) Enhancing employee productivity in terms of quality.
(IV) Higher profits resulting from enhanced productivity.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
B. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
C. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
D. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

An organisation is reviewing two employee-learning interventions. Intervention P is intended to increase employees’ knowledge and skills so that they can perform their present jobs better. Intervention Q is intended to support employees’ overall learning and growth and is career-oriented. Treat these descriptions as the intended purposes of the interventions.

Consider the following statements:
(A) P is development because increasing knowledge and skills is the defining feature of development.
(B) P is training because it is intended to help employees do their jobs better.
(C) Q is training because it is intended to help employees perform their present jobs better.
(D) Q is development because it is intended to support employees’ overall growth.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(A) (A) and (C) only
(B) (B) and (D) only
(C) (A) and (D) only
(D) (B) and (C) only

Two selected employees, P and Q, attend the same induction. During it, each is introduced to the other employees and familiarised with the organisation’s rules and policies. P is occupying the post for which P was selected, while Q has not begun occupying the post for which Q was selected. Which conclusion follows?

A business proposes three measures in its staffing plan: avoiding overmanning, indicating personnel shortages in advance, and objectively assessing employee contributions before giving fair rewards. Each statement below claims a link between a measure and an organisational benefit. Consider the following statements:
(A) Avoiding overmanning is linked to preventing under-utilisation of personnel and high labour costs.
(B) Advance indication of personnel shortages is linked to preventing under-utilisation and high labour costs, rather than to avoiding disruption of work.
(C) Objective assessment and fair rewards for contribution are linked to improved job satisfaction and morale.
(D) Objective assessment and fair rewards are linked to indicating shortages in advance and avoiding disruption of work.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

ideas.body: A department manager who is not in a position titled “supervisor” observes the ongoing work of subordinate employees, guides their efforts and gives them instructions. Which understanding of supervision best describes these actions?
An organisation introduces a suitable monetary and non-monetary reward plan. An employee believes that their efforts will bring suitable rewards. Which response is supported by this situation?

A manager plans to introduce a new accounting system. Arrange the following events in the order described in this situation.
(A) The manager provides training and motivates the staff with additional rewards.
(B) Employees may accept the change and cooperate with the manager.
(C) Accounting staff show initial resistance to the proposed system.
(D) The manager explains the purpose of the proposed system.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Case: A manager is introducing a new accounting system, and staff show initial resistance. Match each need or objective in List-I with the corresponding managerial response in List-II.
List-I
(A) Staff do not understand why the system is being introduced.
(B) Staff need help adapting to the new system.
(C) Staff need encouragement to accept the change.
(D) The manager aims to reduce resistance and develop cooperation.
List-II
(I) Motivate staff with additional rewards.
(II) Explain the purpose of the change.
(III) Use effective directing through motivation, communication and leadership.
(IV) Provide training.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Employees initially oppose a needed change in the organisation.
(B) The manager explains the change, provides training, and uses motivation and leadership.
(C) After the manager’s intervention, employees accept the change and cooperate in introducing it.
(D) Cooperation and commitment among people across groups help the organisation remain steady and balanced.

List-II
(I) A tendency to resist organisational change
(II) Directing used to reduce resistance and develop cooperation
(III) Acceptance of change and cooperation in its introduction
(IV) Stability and balance associated with cooperation and commitment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A manager instructs, guides, counsels, motivates and leads people in the organisation to achieve its objectives. Which managerial function names this process?

At a service centre, a manager tells staff the service target, explains the tasks, guides and counsels employees who encounter difficulty, encourages them to contribute effort, and leads the team towards the target. Which interpretation best captures the manager's role in this situation?

A manager observes that employees have completed their separate assignments, but their efforts are directed towards conflicting priorities and are not contributing to the department’s shared target. The manager explains how each person’s work should connect with colleagues’ contributions and the organisational target. Which importance of directing is most directly illustrated?

At a manufacturing unit, the plant manager sends two shift supervisors the same message, which only reports the organisational output objective and gives no task instructions. Supervisor X gives the team work instructions, guides task performance, counsels a hesitant worker, motivates the team and leads its effort towards the objective. Supervisor Y forwards the message verbatim and has no further interaction with the team. Considering each supervisor’s interaction with the respective shift team, which assessment best applies the meaning of directing?

A manager wants to introduce a new system of accounting, and the accounting staff initially resist the change. Which action combines the measures described as helping employees accept the change and cooperate with the manager?

A distribution firm introduces a needed change to its order-routing procedure. The dispatch team initially resists. The manager uses communication, leadership and motivation; the team then accepts the change and cooperates in introducing it. The case states that cooperation and commitment among other groups have not developed and balance among departments has not yet been achieved. Which conclusion is best supported?

Consider two situations. In each, a manager guides and counsels staff, motivates them and leads their efforts. In Case X, these actions are directed towards an organisational objective. In Case Y, their sole intended aim is the manager’s personal objective, expressly unrelated to any organisational objective. Which statements are correct?
(A) Case X is consistent with directing because the actions are used to lead people towards an organisational objective.
(B) Case Y is necessarily directing too, because using these actions is sufficient regardless of the intended objective.
(C) Case X is not merely communication, since motivation and leadership are among the elements encompassed by directing.
(D) In Case X, guiding and counselling fall outside directing; only motivation and leadership can be part of it.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A management trainee is given five activities associated with directing: (A) motivating employees, (B) instructing employees, (C) leading employees, (D) counselling employees and (E) guiding employees. Arrange them in the order in which they are listed in the standard definition of directing.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
(A) (B)-(D)-(E)-(A)-(C)
(B) (E)-(B)-(D)-(A)-(C)
(C) (B)-(E)-(D)-(A)-(C)
(D) (B)-(E)-(A)-(D)-(C)

A firm introduces a needed organisational change. In this case, employees initially resist it; effective directing through communication, motivation and leadership is then used to reduce resistance and develop cooperation. Arrange the following events in the order described, ending with the organisational outcome associated with cooperation and commitment.
(A) Cooperation and commitment help foster stability and balance in the organisation.
(B) Employees initially resist the needed change.
(C) Effective directing through communication, motivation and leadership is used to reduce resistance and develop cooperation.
(D) The firm introduces a needed organisational change.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

A unit supervisor is guiding subordinates’ efforts towards a work target. Arrange the following components in the order in which the supervisory process and its purpose are described. For this question, the sequence is the order of description; the intended results need not occur at separate times.
(A) Work targets are achieved.
(B) The work being done by subordinates is overseen.
(C) Instructions are given to subordinates.
(D) Resources are utilised optimally.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

At a packaging unit, the manager tells operators what tasks to perform, when to perform them and how, then checks whether the instructions are being carried out as intended. Which statements correctly describe the directing shown here?
(A) Directing includes communicating what work is to be done, when it is to be done and how it is to be done.
(B) Directing includes seeing that instructions are implemented in the proper perspective.
(C) Checking implementation is outside directing and belongs only to planning.
(D) Implementation of instructions has no bearing on directing’s contribution to efficient and effective functioning.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

To help employees achieve organisational objectives, a manager’s directing process includes the elements below. Arrange the elements in the order in which they are named in the definition of directing.
(A) Motivating
(B) Instructing
(C) Leading
(D) Guiding
(E) Counselling
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

A logistics firm proposes a needed change to its parcel-sorting workflow. Employees initially resist it. The manager wants to use effective directing to reduce resistance and develop cooperation. Which response is most consistent with this role of directing?

Treat supervision here as an element of directing. A unit meets its work target but uses more materials than necessary. Its manager oversees subordinate employees’ ongoing work and instructs them to use materials efficiently while maintaining the target. Which supervisory purpose is most directly illustrated?

A textile unit offers an employee a motivation plan with suitable monetary and non-monetary rewards. Assume the employee then believes that their efforts will bring suitable rewards. Arrange the following events in the causal order described, ending with the employee’s contribution.
(A) The employee contributes maximum efforts for the organisation.
(B) The employee feels that their efforts will bring suitable rewards.
(C) The unit offers the motivation plan.
(D) The plan motivates the employee.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

At each level of a three-level reporting chain, assume that a manager first receives instructions from their immediate boss and then directs their immediate subordinate. The reporting chain is Director, Manager, Team leader, and Operator, in that order. Arrange the interactions from first to last.
(A) The team leader directs the operator.
(B) The manager receives instructions from the director.
(C) The manager directs the team leader.
(D) The team leader receives instructions from the manager.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

ideas.body:
A manager sets critical points, focuses attention on significant deviations that cross the permissible limit, and leaves routine problems to subordinates. Consider the following statements about this arrangement:
(A) It can save managers’ time and effort.
(B) It directs managerial attention to routine problems rather than important areas.
(C) It facilitates delegation of authority.
(D) It decreases employee morale.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Consider the following statements about the timing of measuring actual performance:
(A) It is generally believed that measurement should be done after the task is completed.
(B) Wherever possible, measurement of work should be done during performance.
(C) Even where measurement during performance is possible, measurement should be done only after the task is completed.
(D) Measurement should be done during performance for every task, whether or not such measurement is possible.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A manager finds that output in a critical area has fallen significantly beyond its permissible limit. The cause has not yet been established. Which response should guide the manager’s next step?

A manager's control report identifies a significant deviation beyond the permissible limit in a designated critical result area. The report does not establish its cause. What should the manager do next?

A manager identifies a production indicator as a critical point and sets a permissible limit for it. During review, one deviation is within the limit and routine in nature; another is significant and exceeds the limit. The manager intends to apply management by exception. Which statements are correct?
(A) Every departure from the standard must be referred to the manager, even when it remains within the permissible limit.
(B) The significant deviation that exceeds the permissible limit should be brought to the manager’s notice.
(C) The routine problem should be left to subordinates.
(D) Once a significant deviation is referred to the manager, its cause need not be analysed.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company is introducing a control process for the time taken to process online orders. The actions are listed below. Assume the comparison reveals a gap requiring corrective action. What is the correct sequence?
P. Examine the reasons for any gap
Q. Set a benchmark for processing time
R. Take corrective action
S. Measure actual processing time
T. Compare actual processing time with the benchmark

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Actual results are consolidated in performance reports.
(B) A standard is stated as defects per 1,000 units, and actual defects are recorded per 1,000 units.
(C) During an assembling task, each part is checked as it is produced.
(D) A manager requires the measure of actual performance to be objective and reliable.

List-II
(I) Use a stated technique for measuring actual performance.
(II) Use the same units for actual performance and the standard.
(III) Measure work during performance where possible.
(IV) Ensure that actual performance is measured objectively and reliably.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company identifies machine downtime as a critical point in a key result area. The standard is 100 minutes per shift. Deviations of up to and including 5% from the standard are permissible; any deviation greater than 5% is significant. In one shift, the recorded deviations are: P, 4% above the standard; Q, 6% above the standard; R, 5% below the standard; and S, 8% above the standard. The company has designated S's deviation as major. Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) P should be reported to management because any departure from the standard must be escalated.
(B) Q should be reported to management because its deviation is beyond the permissible limit.
(C) R should be reported because a deviation exactly at the permissible limit is beyond that limit.
(D) S requires immediate management action on a priority basis because its deviation is classified as major.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A manager is monitoring an assembling task. Each part can be checked while it is being produced, so measurement during the task is feasible. Select the statements that correctly apply the rule that, wherever possible, work should be measured during performance.
(A) The manager should measure the work while the task is in progress.
(B) The manager should measure actual performance only after the task is complete.
(C) Checking each part as it is produced is an example of measuring work during performance.
(D) Measurement during performance is suitable only for assembling tasks.

A manager is controlling one critical result area. Arrange the following actions in the correct sequence:
(A) The plan specifies the permissible range for the result area.
(B) A significant deviation beyond the permissible limit is identified.
(C) The deviation is brought to management’s notice.
(D) If the deviation is major, it receives immediate action on a priority basis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm has designated process temperature as a critical point. Its standard is 80°C, and the permissible variation is ±2°C. The current deviation from the standard is +6°C, which the firm classifies as major. All other tracked measures are within their permissible ranges. Which action best follows the firm’s control arrangement?

A quality-control manager has set a standard of no more than 6 defective units per 1,000 units produced. During one shift, 2,400 units are produced and 12 are defective. Assume the 2,400 units are the full output covered by the standard for that shift, and the 12 defective units are the complete count for that output. Which comparison of actual performance with the standard is correct?

A manufacturing unit has set a permissible limit for machine downtime in a key result area designated as critical. In one shift, downtime exceeds that limit, and the deviation is brought to the manager’s notice. No investigation has yet established its cause. What is the most appropriate next step?
A service team sets a standard processing time of 90 minutes per batch. It records actual time as 1.5 hours per batch. Before comparing the two results, what should the manager do?

ideas.body:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Estimating funds required for long-term assets
(B) Estimating when funds must be available
(C) Specifying possible sources of funds
(D) Dealing with surplus funds
List-II
(I) Put the surplus to the best possible use
(II) Identify where funds may be obtained
(III) Determine the time when funds are needed
(IV) Estimate the amount required for long-term assets
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Cost reduction in procurement
(B) Risk control
(C) Effective deployment of funds
(D) Fund availability without idleness
List-II
(I) Keep the risk associated with finance under control
(II) Have enough funds whenever needed while avoiding idle funds
(III) Lower the cost incurred in obtaining funds
(IV) Put funds to effective use
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR)
(B) Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR)
(C) Return on Investment (RoI)
(D) Cost of debt
List-II
(I) A higher value indicates lower risk of failing to meet interest payments, but this measure does not capture a low cash balance or repayment obligations.
(II) Cash profits from operations are compared with the total cash required to service debt and preference share capital; this measure addresses the stated deficiencies of the interest-based ratio.
(III) A higher value can support the use of trading on equity to increase EPS; this factor concerns the company’s return from investment.
(IV) A lower rate at which the firm can borrow increases its capacity to employ debt.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company makes a financial decision whose benefit exceeds its cost. Arrange the following events in the cause-and-effect order implied by the financial-management objective, not by elapsed time:
(A) Shareholders gain.
(B) Value addition takes place.
(C) The market price of equity shares increases.
(D) The benefit from the decision exceeds its cost.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

A company is considering an expansion. Workstream X compares the costs and benefits of the available investment and financing alternatives and recommends one with the objective of increasing shareholders’ wealth. Once that decision is made, Workstream Y forecasts which items are likely to change as operations expand, estimates the resulting fund requirements in amount and timing, and anticipates shortages or surpluses so that action can be taken in advance to support smooth operations. Which classification correctly identifies X and Y, respectively?

Four firms propose investing procured funds as follows. For every firm, the procurement cost and expected investment return are annual percentages calculated on the same basis, and no other costs or returns affect the comparison.
Firm P: procurement cost 8%; expected return 7%.
Firm Q: procurement cost 9%; expected return 9%.
Firm R: procurement cost 10%; expected return 11%.
Firm S: procurement cost 12%; expected return 11%.
Which firm's proposal satisfies the requirement that the return from procured finance exceed its procurement cost?

A firm's projected cash remaining after normal business operations and planned fixed-asset investment is ₹12,00,000 for the coming quarter. Interest and principal payments on its existing debt for that quarter total ₹12,00,000. A proposed loan would add ₹2,00,000 of interest and principal payments due in the same quarter. Assume the loan proceeds are fully committed to the asset project and cannot be used for debt service, and no other cash inflow or reserve is available. Which assessment is best supported by the projected cash-flow position?

A firm increases its use of debt in its capital structure, with no change in its equity funding. Arrange the following from the financing change to a possible severe consequence. The sequence does not imply that default actually occurs.
(A) A default in meeting the debt commitments may force the business into liquidation.
(B) The increased use of debt raises the firm’s fixed financial charges.
(C) The firm increases its use of debt.
(D) The rise in financial risk represents a greater chance of failing to meet payment obligations.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

A business is considering two available sources of finance. Source X has a lower cost but greater associated risk than Source Y; Source Y has a higher cost but lower associated risk. Which statement correctly describes how the business should compare the sources for optimal procurement?
(A) Compare the sources only by cost.
(B) Compare the sources only by associated risk.
(C) Note that both sources are available without comparing their costs or associated risks.
(D) Compare the sources by both cost and associated risk.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company replaces part of its equity financing with borrowed funds while keeping total capital unchanged. The cost of borrowed funds is lower than the cost of equity, and the cost of equity is assumed to remain unaffected by the change. No other financing terms change. What is the likely effect on the company’s overall cost of capital?

A company considering new borrowing prepares a cash-flow forecast that includes payments for normal business operations and investment in fixed assets. It excludes interest and principal repayments on the proposed borrowing and includes no buffer after fixed cash-payment obligations. Which statements correctly describe what the company should consider before borrowing?
(A) The forecast is sufficient to assess borrowing capacity because it includes operating and fixed-asset payments.
(B) The company should include the proposed interest and principal repayments among the cash-payment commitments considered.
(C) The projected cash flows should provide a buffer after covering the relevant fixed cash-payment obligations.
(D) The company may omit principal repayment because only interest is a debt-service cash commitment.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm has scarce funds and must select one of four mutually exclusive asset proposals. The forecasts are comparable estimates of return to the firm’s investors. Proposal P is expected to yield a higher return than Q; R is expected to yield a higher return than P; and S is expected to yield a lower return than Q. No other selection criterion is supplied. Which proposal should the firm choose to seek the highest possible return for investors?

A firm has procured ₹20,00,000 for one year at an annual procurement cost of ₹1,60,000. It will invest the entire amount in exactly one of four projects. The stated annual investment returns are: Project P, ₹1,80,000; Project Q, ₹1,60,000; Project R, ₹1,55,000; and Project S, ₹1,50,000. Assume these are directly comparable annual amounts. Which project meets the condition that the return from the investment exceeds the cost of procuring the finance?

A company must choose exactly one of three mutually exclusive alternatives. The finance team estimates their effects on the current market value of equity shares, including all relevant costs and benefits, on the same basis: A, +₹8 lakh; B, +₹5 lakh; C, –₹12 lakh. Assume these estimates are reliable. Consider the following statements:
(A) Alternative A is the best choice for maximising shareholders’ wealth among these alternatives.
(B) Alternative B is equally good as A because both are projected to increase market value.
(C) Alternative C is the best choice because its projected change has the greatest absolute size.
(D) Selecting the best available alternative makes the decision efficient.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company is considering taking additional debt. The new debt will create regular interest payments and a principal repayment obligation. Which projected-cash check directly addresses the outflows created by this borrowing?

A. Confirm that projected cash will cover the added interest payments and principal repayment.
B. Confirm that projected cash will cover the added interest payments but exclude principal repayment.
C. Confirm that projected cash will cover the added principal repayment but exclude interest payments.
D. Confirm that projected cash will cover normal operations but exclude both debt payments.

ideas.body:
Consider the following independent cases:
(A) Company M issues securities and raises capital through that issuance.
(B) Company N issues securities, but the issuance raises no capital for the company.
(C) Company P raises capital by issuing securities.
(D) Company Q raises capital through a loan and does not issue securities.
Which cases illustrate the primary market objective of allowing companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A securities-desk trainee is classifying share transactions. In each record, the named seller or transferor is the person from whom the recipient obtains the shares. Which record belongs to the secondary market?

Consider the following transactions. Each transaction concerns shares or securities; the individuals are investors, and the company described as issuing the shares is the issuer.
(A) Meera buys shares from another individual investor.
(B) An issuing company sells shares directly to Meera.
(C) Meera sells securities to another individual investor.
(D) Meera sells shares directly to the company that issued them.
Which of the following statements describe transactions in the secondary market?
A company issues securities to raise funds for a new project. Which objective of the primary market does this illustrate?

A company plans to raise capital by issuing securities in a primary-market transaction. Consider the following statements about the objective served by this plan:
(A) The plan uses a route through which the primary market allows companies to raise capital.
(B) In the objective described, the company is the capital-raising party.
(C) The objective described is to enable investors, rather than companies, to raise capital through securities issuance.
(D) Under the objective described, the company raises capital without issuing securities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Asha is considering four separate purchases of shares. Company Z is the issuer of the shares, Ravi is an investor who holds shares, and the named seller in each option is the actual seller. Which purchase is in the secondary market?

Company K is the issuer of a security. Riya, Kabir, Meera and Omar are investors. The following transfers of the same security are listed in shuffled order. There were no other transfers, and each seller must first acquire the security before transferring it.
(A) Kabir transfers the security to Meera.
(B) Company K transfers the security to Riya.
(C) Meera transfers the security to Omar.
(D) Riya transfers the security to Kabir.
Arrange the transfers from earliest to latest, beginning with the issuer’s transfer and ending with Omar’s acquisition.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

The stages below describe one company’s single capital-raising episode. Arrange them from the initial aim to the completed outcome.
(A) The company seeks to raise capital.
(B) The company issues securities in the primary market.
(C) The company raises capital through the issuance.
Choose the correct sequence from the options below:
A student is classifying four share transactions. In each option, the named parties are the parties directly involved. Which transaction takes place in the secondary market?
Mira, an investor, buys shares from another investor who already owns them. The issuing company is not a party to the sale. Which classification applies to this transaction?

Northstar Ltd needs funds. Under Plan 1, it issues new securities to investors and receives their payments. Under Plan 2, an existing investor transfers already-issued securities to another investor, and the payment goes to the selling investor, not Northstar Ltd. Which assessment best applies the objective of the primary market?
A company issues new securities to obtain funds for expanding its operations. Which interpretation best describes the objective illustrated by this case?

Arjun, an investor, owns shares that have already been issued. Nisha, also an investor, buys those shares directly from Arjun. Arjun receives the payment, and the issuer is not a party to this transaction. Which description is correct?

Consider the following statements about one main objective of the primary market:
I. It is to enable companies to raise capital through issuing securities.
II. It is to enable investors to raise capital through issuing securities.
III. It is to enable companies to raise capital through purchasing securities.
IV. It is to enable companies to invest capital through issuing securities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Kaveri Ltd needs additional funds and is comparing the following transactions. Which transaction directly achieves the primary market’s objective of enabling a company to raise capital through securities?

Match List-I with List-II. All named persons other than “the issuer” are investors, and each entry describes a single transaction in shares or securities with the stated counterparty.

List-I
(A) Investor P buys shares from Investor Q.
(B) Investor R sells shares to Investor S.
(C) Investor T buys shares from the issuer.
(D) Investor V sells shares to the issuer.

List-II
(I) Secondary-market purchase
(II) Secondary-market sale
(III) Investor purchase from the issuer
(IV) Investor sale to the issuer

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Company Q is the issuer of the shares. It first issues shares to Aruna, an investor. Later, Aruna transfers part of her holding to Bala, an investor; Bala transfers some of those shares to Charu, an investor; and Charu sells shares to Company Q. Each transaction is direct between the named parties, and each concerns shares. Match each transaction in List-I with its description in List-II. Determine only whether each transaction fits the secondary-market definition.
List-I
(A) Company Q first issues shares to Aruna.
(B) Aruna transfers shares to Bala.
(C) Bala transfers shares to Charu.
(D) Charu sells shares to Company Q.
List-II
(I) The issuer supplies shares to an investor; the transaction is not between investors.
(II) Aruna supplies shares to Bala; both are investors.
(III) Bala supplies shares to Charu; both are investors.
(IV) Charu supplies shares to the issuer; the transaction is not between investors.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Use this stated objective: “One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities.” Match each statement in List-I with its interpretation in List-II.

List-I
(A) Companies may raise capital through the issuance of securities.
(B) Every company seeking to raise capital must issue securities.
(C) Issuance of securities is the sole route by which companies can raise capital.
(D) Issuing securities cannot enable companies to raise capital.

List-II
(I) Expresses the stated enabling link.
(II) Claims that securities issuance is necessary whenever a company seeks capital.
(III) Claims that securities issuance is the only route to raise capital.
(IV) Denies the stated enabling link.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct mapping for each transaction.
List-I
(A) Zenith Ltd issues a batch of shares directly to Riya.
(B) Riya sells the shares she received to Samir.
(C) Samir sells those same shares to Tara.
(D) Zenith Ltd issues a separate batch of shares directly to Tara.
List-II
(I) Secondary-market acquisition by Tara from Samir.
(II) Secondary-market acquisition by Samir from Riya.
(III) Riya’s direct acquisition from Zenith Ltd.
(IV) Tara’s direct acquisition from Zenith Ltd.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Company Z, the issuer, initially issues a security to investor A. Later, A sells the same security to investor B. A and B are investors, and Company Z is not a party to the later sale. How should the later sale be classified?
A company needs funds for its own expansion and is comparing the following plans. Which plan most directly fits the objective of the company raising capital through the issuance of securities?

ideas.body:
Using the standard four-P sequence of the marketing mix, arrange the following elements:
(A) Place
(B) Promotion
(C) Product
(D) Price
Choose the correct sequence.

A firm has manufactured a product. It completes packaging, branding, pricing and promotion before dispatching the product. In this workflow, physical movement from the place of production to the place of distribution is completed before the product is recorded as available to customers. Treat each description below as a separate stage and arrange the stages from first to last.
(A) The product is available to customers at the right place, in the right quantity and at the right time.
(B) The product is manufactured.
(C) The product is packaged, branded, priced and promoted.
(D) The product is physically handled and moved from production to distribution.
Choose the correct sequence from the options below:

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) A firm has a larger number of warehouses serving customers at different locations.
(B) An agricultural product requires long-term storage.
(C) A product, such as machinery, is bulky and difficult to ship.
(D) A product, such as bakery goods, is perishable.

List-II
(I) A larger warehouse count is generally associated with less time to serve customers at different locations and greater warehousing cost.
(II) Warehouses are located near production sites to help minimise charges on transporting the goods.
(III) Warehouses are placed at different locations near the market in view of bulk and shipping difficulty.
(IV) Warehouses are placed at different locations near the market for a perishable product.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match each situation in List-I with the most directly relevant distribution responsibility in List-II. Treat each situation as a separate issue, and use each entry in List-II once.

List-I
(A) A customer seeks a product at a retail outlet, but it is unavailable there and the customer may buy an alternative brand.
(B) Production is seasonal, while the sale or use of the goods occurs later, creating a time gap.
(C) Users are widely spread and geographically separated from the place of production.
(D) The firm must decide whether to use wholesalers, retailers, or both as intermediaries.

List-II
(I) Moving goods to the place where they are needed for consumption or use
(II) Storing goods to maintain a smooth flow between production or procurement and sale or use
(III) Selecting channels of distribution
(IV) Making goods physically available where customers want to buy them

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Physical product
(B) Benefit from the customer’s viewpoint
(C) Extended product
(D) Product decisions

List-II
(I) Decisions about features, quality, packaging, labelling and branding
(II) An item offered, such as televisions, refrigerators and colour monitors
(III) The result sought by buying toothpaste, such as whitening teeth or strengthening gums
(IV) After-sales services, handling complaints and availability of spare parts

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A firm uses intermediaries to make its product available to buyers. Which intermediary activity is specifically identified as taking place after a sale?

A firm must choose a site for a warehouse used to store an agricultural product for a long period. Its stated objective in this decision is to minimise the transportation charges on the goods. Which location best fits this objective?
A company wants its products to be available to target customers in several towns. Which plan directly addresses this objective through Place or physical distribution?

A manufacturer produces a household product at one site, while its customers are spread across distant markets. The firm is deciding which mode to use to move the product from the production site to those markets, considering the product’s nature, cost and target-market locations. It is not reconsidering its marketing intermediaries or the stock levels to maintain. Which decision area is the firm addressing?

A firm serves customers at several locations and is deciding how many warehouses to operate. It also stores a product that requires long-term storage. Consider the following statements:
(A) Warehousing may be needed when the time of production differs from the time the product is required for consumption.
(B) Increasing the number of warehouses generally reduces the time taken to serve customers at different locations but increases warehousing cost.
(C) To minimise transportation charges for the long-term-storage product, the firm should locate its warehouses near the markets.
(D) The firm should balance warehousing cost against the level of customer service when deciding on its warehouses.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A manufacturer sells its product through independent local dealers and wants to improve its availability to target customers through this network. It must choose one action. Which action is a Place or physical-distribution decision for this objective?

A firm is reviewing how to describe its toothpaste and refrigerator offerings. Consider the following statements:
(A) Toothpaste benefits such as whitening teeth and strengthening gums are part of the product concept.
(B) For a refrigerator, after-sales services, handling complaints and availability of spare parts can be part of the extended product.
(C) Because a refrigerator is a physical good, its product concept excludes after-sales services and availability of spare parts.
(D) The extended-product aspect is particularly important for consumer durables such as refrigerators.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm uses personal selling. A case traces the societal effects attributed to this activity. Arrange the stages from the initial activity to the broader outcome.
(A) Economic growth is influenced.
(B) Economic activity in society is fostered.
(C) More jobs, more incomes and more products and services follow.
(D) Personal selling is undertaken.
Choose the correct sequence.

A manufacturer’s catalogue identifies steel, trucks and salt as its offerings, alongside other products. A reviewer claims that one manufacturer can have only one product, so the three named offerings cannot all count as its products. Which conclusion is supported?
A firm has set sales and profit objectives and is comparing complete marketing mixes. Which criterion should it use to identify the most effective combination of marketing elements?

A firm serves several towns from its warehouses. The same product, with the same storage requirement and equal inventory, is held at each warehouse; the total warehouse count is fixed. Customer-service efficiency differs across towns. Which comparison most directly addresses a warehouse-related factor that could explain this difference?

A wholesaler stores an adequate stock of goods. Deliveries to the wholesaler are subject to unavoidable delays, while demand remains at its forecast level. Which purpose of storing adequate stock is illustrated?

A firm receives finished goods at a storage facility. Staff assign each batch to a storage bay and keep it there. Stock-level decisions and physical movement to distribution points are handled separately. Which basic warehousing purpose is illustrated?

ideas.body: For this question, a complainant may be one or more consumers, a voluntary consumer association, the Central or a State Government, the Central Authority, a legal heir or legal representative, or a parent or legal representative in the case of a minor. A complaint is an allegation in writing by a complainant seeking relief concerning a restrictive trade practice, a defect in goods, deficiency in services, overcharging, or goods or services injurious to life and safety. Which case satisfies both definitions?

A minor consumer is involved in a complaint concerning a school bag, and the minor’s parent proposes to file on the minor’s behalf. Separately, an adult consumer who bought a home appliance for household use has died, and that consumer’s legal heir proposes to file a complaint. The people and entities named in options B–D are not consumers, voluntary consumer associations, central or state governments, the central authority, legal heirs, legal representatives, or parents or legal representatives in a minor’s case. Which proposed pair consists of two categories included in the definition of “complainant”?

A wholesaler keeps its posted unit price unchanged but deliberately holds back part of its stock from distribution, thereby reducing the flow of supplies. Consumers consequently pay an additional amount elsewhere for the same goods; the case stipulates that this additional cost is unjustified. The goods have no fault or inadequacy in quality, nature or performance, and no fault or omission in any service is involved. Which concept best classifies the wholesaler’s conduct?

A home-appliance firm, facing strong competition and seeking to increase sales and market share, plans to advertise a model as safe while continuing to sell units from a batch that its own testing has identified as unsafe. Assume the safety finding and the misleading nature of the planned claim are as stated. Which conclusion best applies the concept of consumer protection to this decision?

A consumer association finds widespread ignorance about consumers’ rights and available reliefs. It plans an educational initiative specifically to achieve consumer awareness. Arrange the following stages in the logical order from problem identification to intended outcome.
(A) Consumers attain awareness of their rights and available reliefs.
(B) Widespread ignorance of consumers about their rights and available reliefs is identified.
(C) Consumers are educated about those rights and reliefs.

A business uses resources that belong to society to make a household appliance. It can choose between two voluntary manufacturing practices: Practice X does not meet the needs and interests expressed by customers, while Practice Y does. The business chooses Practice Y, which is stated to serve the public interest and not impair public confidence. Which statement best explains how this choice relates to the business’s responsibility arising from its use of society’s resources?

Meera is using a household product. Before using it, she reads and follows the manufacturer’s instructions. She continues to acquire knowledge about products over time and aims to remain well informed throughout life.

Consider the following statements:
(A) Meera’s use of the manufacturer’s instructions is consistent with using the product safely.
(B) The guidance treats acquiring knowledge as a task completed once, rather than continued throughout life.
(C) Continuing to acquire knowledge is consistent with becoming well informed throughout life.
(D) The guidance treats access to manufacturer’s instructions and acquiring knowledge as alternatives, so a consumer needs only one of them.

Which statements are supported by the guidance described?
(A) (A) and (B) only
(B) (B) and (D) only
(C) (A) and (D) only
(D) (A) and (C) only

A batch of sealed products is sold under its genuine brand. Testing shows that the products do not meet the prescribed quality standards. The products are not counterfeit or duplicate, and no inferior substance has been added. Which practice best describes this sale?

Match each case in List-I with the appropriate forum in List-II. Assume that each complaint is otherwise maintainable and that its stated amount is the value of goods or services paid as consideration. Each appeal is lodged within 30 days of the challenged order.

List-I
(A) An original complaint involving consideration of ₹50 lakh
(B) An original complaint involving consideration of ₹1 crore
(C) An appeal against an order of the State Commission
(D) An appeal against an order of the National Commission

List-II
(I) National Commission
(II) Supreme Court of India
(III) District Commission
(IV) State Commission

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A consumer buys an appliance, receives a cash memo and discovers a shortcoming in its quality. The amount involved is stipulated to be small: ₹800. Consider the following statements about the consumer’s actions:
(A) The cash memo can serve as proof of the purchase.
(B) A complaint to an appropriate consumer forum is warranted only if the amount involved is substantial.
(C) A shortcoming in the quality of goods is a stated reason to file a complaint in an appropriate consumer forum.
(D) The consumer should not refrain from taking action merely because the amount involved is small.
Which option identifies the correct statements?

Riya is selecting a household product and will then use it. Arrange the following consumer responsibilities in the order that moves from making an informed market choice to selecting a product and then using it safely.
(A) Be aware of the goods and services available in the market so that an intelligent and wise choice can be made.
(B) Buy only standardised goods.
(C) Learn about risks associated with the product, follow the manufacturer’s instructions and use it safely.
Choose the correct order from the options given below:

Arrange the events in chronological order in one continuing case. The National Commission’s order is on the appeal from the State Commission, and the Supreme Court appeal challenges that National Commission order. Each appeal is filed within 30 days of the order challenged.
(A) The National Commission issues its order on the appeal.
(B) The State Commission issues its order.
(C) An appeal is filed with the Supreme Court against the National Commission’s order.
(D) An appeal is filed with the National Commission against the State Commission’s order.
Choose the correct sequence:

Match each concern in List-I to the consumer right in List-II that corresponds most directly. Use the ordinary meaning of the right names.

List-I
(A) Product safety
(B) Product particulars
(C) Choice among alternatives
(D) Views listened to

List-II
(I) Right to choose
(II) Right to safety
(III) Right to be heard
(IV) Right to be informed

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A retailer in a consumer market tells buyers that the market still follows “buyer beware”, so sellers need not be watchful of consumer interests. Which description best corrects this claim?
A consumer organisation wants to give buyers a basis for comparing the relative qualities of competing brands. Which proposed activity most directly serves this aim?

Match each entity or consumer description in List-I with its directly stated role in List-II.
List-I
(A) Business associations such as FICCI and CII
(B) Consumer organisations
(C) A well-informed consumer
(D) Government
List-II
(I) Protects consumer interests by enacting measures
(II) Lays down members’ guidelines for dealings with customers
(III) Is positioned to raise a voice against unfair trade practices or exploitation
(IV) Educates consumers about their rights and provides protection
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A consumer is dissatisfied with a service and files a complaint. It has not yet been established whether the service falls short of expectations. Which conclusion follows about the consumer’s right to be heard and seek redressal?
